80345.e: Whatever soaks into the ground can reach the groundwater. That is why you must never pour poison or oil onto the ground.
80345.m: Poison in the soil can pollute groundwater.

80346.q: How did people long ago get water up from a deep well?
a: With a bucket on a rope
80346.e: A well like this reaches down to the groundwater. People lowered a bucket on a rope and pulled it back up full of water.
80346.m: People used to get well water up with a bucket.

80347.q: Where in the ground is groundwater usually found?
a: In gaps between gravel and sand
In big caves full of air
80347.e: Groundwater fills the tiny spaces between small stones, gravel and sand. There is usually no open underground lake.
80347.m: Groundwater is in the gaps between gravel and sand.

a: Yes, as fast as a river
80348.e: Groundwater moves slowly through the ground, often only a few metres a day. It flows towards rivers or lakes.

80349.q: What happens to groundwater if it does not rain for a very long time?
a: It gets as warm as a bath
80349.e: Without rain, no new water comes in. The water table then slowly drops.
80349.m: In a drought, the groundwater sinks.

a: When the ground is completely dry
80350.e: Rainwater flows into small dips in the ground. If it cannot soak away quickly, a puddle is left.
80350.m: Puddles collect in dips after rain.

80351.q: Why do puddles on tarmac stay for a long time?
a: Tarmac does not let water through
80351.e: Tarmac is sealed, so the water cannot soak into the ground. It stays there until it evaporates or drains away.
80351.m: Tarmac does not let rainwater through.

80352.q: Where does a puddle go on a sunny day?
a: A bird drinks it all up
80352.e: The warmth of the sun makes the water evaporate. It becomes invisible water vapour in the air.

80353.q: What shimmers in a puddle when a little oil is floating on it?
80353.e: A very thin layer of oil on the water makes the light shimmer in bright colours.
80353.m: Oil on a puddle shimmers in many colours.

80354.q: What happens to a puddle on a frosty night?
80354.e: Below 0 degrees, water turns into ice. In the morning the puddle is then often covered with a layer of ice.
80354.m: Puddles freeze when there is frost.

80355.q: Which birds collect wet mud from puddles to build their nests?
80355.e: Swallows make little balls out of damp mud. They use them to stick their nests under a roof, for example.
80355.m: Swallows build their nests from mud.

80356.q: What do you see when you look into a still puddle?
80356.e: The smooth surface of the water reflects the light like a mirror. That is why you see yourself and the sky.
80356.m: A still puddle reflects like a mirror.

80357.q: Which insects like to lay their eggs in puddles and water butts?
80357.e: Mosquitoes need still water for their larvae. Even a small puddle can be enough.
80357.m: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water.

80358.q: Which animals sometimes lay their eggs in puddles in wheel ruts?
80358.e: Some toads, such as the yellow-bellied toad, like small, warm puddles, for example in wheel ruts. They lay their spawn there.
80358.m: Toads also lay their eggs in puddles.

80359.q: On which nights does a lot of dew form?
80359.e: Without clouds, the ground cools down a lot at night. Without wind, the water from the air can then settle easily on the grass.
80359.m: Clear, calm nights bring lots of dew.

80360.q: Where does the water in dewdrops come from?
a: From water vapour in the air
80360.e: There is invisible water vapour in the air. When the air cools down, it turns back into liquid water in small drops.
80360.m: Dew forms from water vapour in the air.

80361.q: What happens to dew when the sun shines in the morning?
a: It turns into fog in the ground
80361.e: The sun warms the grass and the air. The drops then turn back into water vapour.

80362.q: Where do dewdrops glitter especially beautifully in the morning?
80362.e: Lots of little drops hang on the fine threads of a spider's web. In the morning light they glitter like pearls.
80362.m: Dewdrops glitter like pearls on spiders' webs.

80363.q: What happens to cold glasses when you come into a warm room?
a: They steam up with tiny droplets
80363.e: The warm air in the room contains water vapour. On the cold glasses it turns into tiny drops, just like dew.
80363.m: Water droplets form on cold surfaces.

80364.q: On a clear night, when is it usually coolest?
80364.e: The ground cools down all night long. That is why it is usually coldest at sunrise, and there is lots of dew.
80364.m: It is often coolest at sunrise.

80365.q: Why is there often less dew under a tree in the morning?
a: The ground there cools down less
The sun shines there at night
80365.e: The treetop works like a blanket and holds back some warmth. The ground underneath gets less cold, so less dew forms.
80365.m: Under trees it cools down less and there is less dew.

a: Fine ice crystals on branches and grass
80366.e: Hoar frost is made of lots of tiny ice crystals. They grow on trees, fences and grass.
80366.m: Hoar frost is made of fine ice crystals.

80367.q: In what weather does hoar frost form?
a: When it is frosty and the air is damp
When it is hot and sunny
80367.e: Hoar frost forms when it is colder than 0 degrees and the air is damp, for example in fog. The tiny droplets freeze onto everything they touch.
80367.m: Hoar frost needs frost and damp air.

80368.e: The many fine ice crystals scatter the light. That is why hoar frost looks white.

80369.q: In which season do we see hoar frost in Switzerland?
80369.e: Hoar frost needs temperatures below 0 degrees. In Switzerland that happens mainly in winter and on cold autumn nights.
80369.m: You see hoar frost mainly in winter.

80370.q: On which side of the twigs does hoar frost grow most?
a: On the side the wind comes from
On the side facing the ground
80370.e: The wind carries the damp, cold air against the twigs. Where it hits them, the ice crystals grow the most.
80370.m: Hoar frost grows towards the wind.

80371.q: What are the patterns of ice called that grow on cold window panes?
80371.e: On cold panes the moisture freezes into branching patterns. They look like flowers made of ice.
80371.m: Frost flowers are ice patterns on windows.

80372.q: What can happen when a lot of hoar frost hangs on trees?
80372.e: Thick hoar frost can get very heavy. Then the branches bend and some break off.
80372.m: Heavy hoar frost can break branches.

80373.q: What happens to hoar frost when it gets warmer?
80373.e: When the temperature rises above 0 degrees, the ice crystals melt. They often fall off the branches like fine snow, too.
80373.m: Hoar frost melts when it gets warmer.

a: Dripping water freezes bit by bit
80374.e: Water runs down an edge and freezes drop by drop. This makes the icicle longer and longer.

80375.q: Why is it dangerous to walk under big icicles?
80375.e: Big icicles are heavy and pointed. If they come loose, they can hurt people.
80375.m: It is better not to walk under big icicles.

80376.q: In what weather do icicles grow especially well?
a: The sun melts snow, but the air is cold
80376.e: The sun melts some snow on the roof. The water drips down and freezes into ice in the cold air.
80376.m: Icicles grow when melting snow freezes in cold air.

80377.q: Which way do icicles grow on a roof?
80377.e: Because of gravity, the water drips downwards. That is why icicles grow from the top down.

80378.q: What happens to icicles when it thaws?
a: They get as hard as stone
80378.e: When it gets warmer than 0 degrees, the ice melts. The icicles drip and get smaller until they fall off.

80379.q: Why are icicles pointed at the bottom?
a: The least water reaches the bottom
Birds peck them into a point
80379.e: Most of the water freezes further up the icicle. Only a little reaches the tip, so it stays thin.
80379.m: Icicles are thick at the top and pointed at the bottom.

80380.q: Where in nature can very long icicles hang in winter?
80380.e: In winter, water seeps out of cracks in the rocks. It freezes and sometimes forms icicles several metres long.
80380.m: Huge icicles grow on rock faces in winter.

a: A very wet area with soft ground
80381.e: In a bog the ground is full of water and very soft. You can sink into it.
80381.m: A bog is a wet area with soft ground.

80382.q: Which animals like living in a wet bog?
80382.e: In a bog there is lots of water and lots of insects. That is why frogs feel at home there.

80383.q: Why are many bogs in Switzerland protected?
a: Rare plants and animals live there
Lots of vegetables are grown there
The best ski slopes are there
Most of the timber grows there
80383.e: In bogs there are plants and animals that are hardly found anywhere else. That is why many bogs are protected.
80383.m: Bogs are home to rare plants and animals.

80384.q: Which small meat-eating plant grows in Swiss bogs?
80384.e: The sundew has sticky drops on its leaves. Small insects get stuck to them and are digested.
80384.m: The sundew catches insects with sticky drops.

80385.q: Who decided in 1987 that bogs in Switzerland should be specially protected?
80385.e: In the vote on the Rothenthurm initiative, the people said yes to protecting bogs. Since then this has been in the Federal Constitution.
80385.m: The Swiss people decided to protect bogs in 1987.

80386.q: Why can a bog store so much water?
a: The moss soaks up water like a sponge
The ground is made of hard rock
Lots of big trees grow there
80386.e: Peat moss can hold many times its own weight in water. This is how the bog holds on to lots of water.
80386.m: A bog stores water like a sponge.

80387.q: Why should you stay on the paths in a bog?
a: You can sink in and trample plants
It is warmer on the paths
It is too dark beside the paths
80387.e: The soft ground of the bog cannot hold you everywhere. Also, rare plants grow there that are easily damaged.
80387.m: In a bog, you stay on the paths.

80388.q: What colour is the water in a raised bog often?
80388.e: Substances from dead plants dissolve in the water. They turn it brown like tea.
80388.m: Bog water is often brown like tea.

a: A small, shallow body of still water
80389.e: A pond is small and so shallow that plants often grow right down to the bottom. The water hardly flows.
80389.m: A pond is a small, shallow body of water.

80390.q: Which animals lay their spawn in the pond in spring?
80390.e: Frogs lay their eggs in the water as spawn. The clumps of eggs float in the pond.
80390.m: Frogs lay spawn in the pond in spring.

80391.q: What are young frogs called that still live in the water?
80391.e: Tadpoles hatch from frogspawn. They have a tail and breathe with gills until they become frogs.

80392.q: Which insect with shimmering wings hunts mosquitoes over ponds?
80392.e: Dragonflies are fast fliers and catch other insects in the air. Their larvae live in the water.
80392.m: Dragonflies hunt mosquitoes over the water.

80393.q: Which insect can walk on the surface of the water?
80393.e: The pond skater is very light and has long legs with fine hairs. That is why it does not sink.
80393.m: The pond skater walks on water.

80394.q: Which plant with big round leaves floats on ponds?
80394.e: The water lily has its roots in the mud at the bottom. Its leaves and flowers float on the water.
80394.m: The water lily floats on the pond.

80395.q: Which plant on the edge of a pond has brown heads that look like sausages?
80395.e: The bulrush grows in shallow water at the edge. Its brown heads are full of seeds.
80395.m: The bulrush has brown heads at the water's edge.

80396.q: Why does a pond freeze over faster in winter than a big lake?
a: It is always in a forest
80396.e: A small, shallow pond holds little water. It cools down quickly and therefore freezes over sooner than a big, deep lake.
80396.m: Small, shallow ponds freeze over quickly.

80397.q: Which bird often swims on ponds, with the male having a shiny green head?
80397.e: The mallard is the most common duck in Switzerland. You can recognise the male by its shimmering green head.
80397.m: The male mallard has a green head.

80398.q: Why can you not drink seawater?
80398.e: Seawater contains a lot of salt. If you drink it, you get even thirstier, because your body has to get rid of the salt.
80398.m: Seawater is too salty to drink.

80399.q: Is there more sea or more land on Earth?
80399.e: Most of the Earth is covered by sea. That is why the Earth is also called the blue planet.
80399.m: Most of the Earth is covered by sea.

80400.q: Which sea does the Rhine flow into in the end?
80400.e: The Rhine flows from Switzerland through Germany and the Netherlands. There it flows into the North Sea.
80400.m: The Rhine flows into the North Sea.

80401.q: Which sea does the Rhône flow into in the end?
80401.e: The Rhône flows through Lake Geneva and then through France. It flows into the Mediterranean in southern France.
80401.m: The Rhône flows into the Mediterranean.

80402.q: Which sea does the water of the Inn from the Engadine reach?
80402.e: The Inn flows into the Danube. The Danube finally flows into the Black Sea.
80402.m: The water of the Inn reaches the Black Sea.

80403.q: What is the largest animal in the sea?
80403.e: The blue whale can grow over 30 metres long. It is even the largest animal that has ever lived on Earth.
80403.m: The blue whale is the largest animal in the world.

80405.q: What do you do with finely chopped red cabbage to get red cabbage juice?
80405.e: The hot water draws the colour out of the leaves. After cooling, you pour the coloured juice through a sieve.
80405.m: Hot water draws the colour out of red cabbage.

80406.q: What colour is red cabbage juice in pure water?
80406.e: In water that is neither acidic nor basic, red cabbage juice is purple. Only when you add something does the colour change.
80406.m: In pure water, red cabbage juice is purple.

80407.q: What colour does red cabbage juice turn when you stir in bicarbonate of soda?
80407.e: Bicarbonate of soda is not acidic but basic. That is why the purple red cabbage juice turns blue to blue-green.
80407.m: Bicarbonate of soda turns red cabbage juice blue.

80408.q: What does red cabbage juice show with its colour?
80408.e: The dye in red cabbage changes colour depending on whether a substance is acidic or basic. This lets you test things from the kitchen.
80408.m: Red cabbage juice shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80409.q: What do you call a substance that shows by its colour whether something is acidic?
80409.e: An indicator is something that shows. Red cabbage juice is an indicator you can make yourself.
80409.m: An indicator shows by its colour whether something is acidic.

80410.q: What does a splash of vinegar do to the colour when cooking red cabbage?
80410.e: Acid from vinegar or sour apples keeps red cabbage red. Without acid it tends to turn bluish when cooked.
80410.m: With a little acid, cooked red cabbage stays red.

80411.q: What property does lemon juice have if it turns red cabbage juice red?
80411.e: Lemon juice contains acid. Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.
80411.m: Acidic substances turn red cabbage juice red.

80412.q: Which juice, like red cabbage juice, changes colour with acid?
80412.e: Blueberries contain a blue dye similar to red cabbage. That is why their juice also changes colour with acid.
80412.m: Blueberry juice also changes colour with acid.

80413.q: What is food colouring used for?
80413.e: Food colouring is safe to eat. It is used, for example, to colour cakes, icing or Easter eggs.

80414.q: Which colour do you get when you mix red and yellow food colouring?
80414.e: Red and yellow together make orange. This way you can mix many new colours from just a few.
80414.m: Red and yellow together make orange.

80415.q: Which vegetable colours food bright red?
80415.e: Beetroot contains a strong red dye. Hands and clothes quickly turn red from it too.

80416.e: Turmeric is a yellow powder made from a root. It colours curries yellow, for example.

80417.q: In which water does a drop of food colouring spread faster?
80417.e: In warm water the tiniest particles move faster. That is why the colour spreads more quickly there.
80417.m: Colour spreads faster in warm water than in cold.

80418.q: What happens to a white flower that stands in water with food colouring for a few days?
a: The flower loses all its leaves
The flower grows twice as big
80418.e: The flower sucks the coloured water up through its stem. This way the colour reaches the flower head.
80418.m: A flower sucks water up through its stem to the flower head.

80419.q: Which vegetable provides a green colouring for food?
80419.e: Spinach contains a lot of green leaf pigment. You can use spinach to colour pasta green, for example.

80420.q: Which letter do the numbers of colourings on packaging start with?
80420.e: Additives such as colourings have an E number on packaging. Colourings have the numbers E 100 to E 199.
80420.m: Colourings are listed on packaging with an E number.

80421.q: You want to separate the colours of a felt-tip pen with water. Which paper do you put the dot of colour on?
80421.e: Coffee filter paper soaks up water well. The water can travel upwards in it and carry the colours with it.
80421.m: To separate colours, you need paper that soaks up water well.

80422.q: A coffee filter with a felt-tip dot stands in water. What travels up the paper and takes the colour with it?
80422.e: The paper soaks water up from the glass. The water dissolves the colour and carries it along.
80422.m: The water carries the colours up the paper.

80423.q: You draw a dot with a black felt-tip pen on a coffee filter and stand it in water. What do you soon see?
a: No colour at all any more
80423.e: Black felt-tip ink is often mixed from several colours. On the paper they separate, for example into blue, yellow and red.
80423.m: Black ink is often mixed from several colours.

80424.q: Where must the dot of colour be on the paper strip when it goes into the water?
80424.e: If the dot is in the water, the colour simply dissolves in the glass. If it is just above, the water rises up to it.
80424.m: The dot of colour must be just above the water.

80425.q: Which pens can you use to separate colours in paper with water?
80425.e: The colour must dissolve in water, otherwise it just stays put. That is why washable felt-tip pens work best.
80425.m: To separate colours with water, you need washable felt-tip pens.

80426.q: What does the Greek word ‘chroma’ in chromatography mean?
80426.e: ‘Chroma’ is the Greek word for colour. So chromatography means roughly ‘colour writing’.

80427.q: A coffee filter with a felt-tip dot stands in water. Why do different stripes of colour appear?
80427.e: Some colours are easily carried along by the water, others tend to stay behind. So they get different distances and separate.
80427.m: Each colour travels a different distance in the paper.

80428.q: Which pigments can you separate from green leaves with chromatography?
80428.e: Green leaves contain not only green but also yellow pigment. With methylated spirits instead of water, and with the help of an adult, you can separate them.
80428.m: Green leaves also contain yellow pigment.

80429.q: What can you use to make a simple invisible ink?
80429.e: Lemon juice is almost colourless and hard to see once dry. That is why it works well as invisible ink.
80429.m: Lemon juice is a simple invisible ink.

80430.q: How do you make writing in lemon juice visible again?
80430.e: When the paper is carefully warmed, for example with an iron, the dried juice changes colour. Only do this with an adult.
80430.m: Heat makes secret writing in lemon juice visible.

80431.q: What colour does lemon juice writing turn when heated?
80431.e: The juice contains sugar and other substances. When heated they turn brown, a bit like toast.

80432.q: Which drink from the fridge can also be an invisible ink?
80432.e: Dried milk is hard to see on white paper. When carefully warmed it turns brown and the writing appears.
80432.m: Milk can also be used as invisible ink.

80433.q: You write with a white candle on white paper. How do you make the writing visible?
80433.e: Wax repels water. The watercolour stays on the paper but not on the wax letters, so they show up light.
80433.m: Wax repels watercolour, so candle writing appears.

80434.q: What is the best thing to write on paper with lemon juice?
80434.e: You dip a cotton bud or a fine brush into the lemon juice and write with it. A pen would leave visible lines.
80434.m: Secret writing in lemon juice is done with a cotton bud or brush.

80435.q: You write with bicarbonate of soda water and then brush red cabbage juice over it. What happens?
80435.e: The bicarbonate of soda changes the colour of the red cabbage juice. That is why the letters appear in a different colour from the rest of the paper.
80435.m: Red cabbage juice can make bicarbonate of soda writing visible.

80436.q: What did people use invisible ink for in the past?
80436.e: With invisible ink, messages could be hidden. Only those who knew how to make it visible could read them.
80436.m: Invisible ink hides messages from prying eyes.

80437.e: Soap is made by boiling fats or oils with an alkali. This boiling is called soap making.
80437.m: Soap is made from fat and alkali.

80438.q: Why do you wash your hands with soap instead of just water?
80438.e: Water alone is poor at rinsing away greasy dirt. Soap wraps up the grease so that the water can rinse it away.
80438.m: Soap helps water rinse away greasy dirt.

80439.q: You sprinkle pepper on water and dip in a finger covered in soap. What does the pepper do?
80439.e: The soap weakens the stretched skin on the surface of the water. The water pulls back towards the edge and takes the pepper with it.
80439.m: Soap weakens the skin on the water.

80440.q: What were the craftsmen who used to make soap called?
80440.e: Soap was boiled in large pots. That is why the craftsmen were called soap boilers.
80440.m: In the past, soap boilers boiled soap in large pots.

80441.q: What forms when you rub soap with a little water between your hands?
80441.e: Soap and water form lots of tiny bubbles when rubbed. You know this white lather from washing your hands.

80442.q: When should you wash your hands with soap especially well?
a: After the toilet and before eating
80442.e: After using the toilet and before eating, clean hands are especially important. That way fewer germs get into your mouth.
80442.m: Wash your hands with soap after the toilet and before eating.

80443.q: A little paper boat has a drop of soap at the back. What happens in the water?
80443.e: The soap weakens the skin on the water at the back. At the front the water pulls more strongly, so the boat moves forwards.
80443.m: A drop of soap can power a paper boat.

80444.q: What happens to a bar of soap that lies in a puddle of water for a long time?
80444.e: Water slowly dissolves the soap at its surface. That is why it is better to let soap dry after washing.
80444.m: Soap in water goes soft and slimy.

80445.q: What is a simple, unscented bar of soap that is also used to wash clothes called?
80445.e: Household soap is a simple, solid soap. It is used, for example, to wash stains out of clothes.
80445.m: Household soap is a simple solid soap.

80446.q: What shape is a soap bubble that floats freely through the air?
80446.e: The thin soap skin pulls itself together as small as possible. The shape with the smallest surface is the sphere.
80446.m: A freely floating soap bubble is perfectly round.

80447.q: What is inside a soap bubble?
80447.e: When you blow, you blow air into the soap skin. Only the thin skin is made of soapy water.
80447.m: A soap bubble is full of air.

80448.q: Why does a soap bubble shimmer in many colours?
a: Light is reflected in the thin skin
80448.e: Light is reflected from the front and back of the thin soap skin. This creates shimmering rainbow colours.
80448.m: The thin skin of a soap bubble makes rainbow colours.

80449.q: What do you add to soapy water so that soap bubbles last longer?
80449.e: Glycerine is a thick, clear liquid. It stops the soap skin from drying out so quickly.
80449.m: Glycerine makes soap bubbles last longer.

80450.q: Why does a soap bubble burst after a while?
80450.e: The water in the soap skin evaporates and flows downwards. When the skin gets too thin, the bubble bursts.
80450.m: A soap bubble bursts when its skin gets too thin.

80451.q: What often happens if you carefully poke a soap bubble with a wet, soapy finger?
80451.e: A dry finger makes the bubble burst. But a finger with soapy water joins up with the soap skin.
80451.m: You can touch a soap bubble with a wet, soapy finger.

80452.q: What can happen to a soap bubble in very cold weather?
80452.e: In hard frost, the water in the soap skin freezes. Then you can see delicate ice patterns on the bubble.
80452.m: In hard frost, soap bubbles can freeze.

80453.q: About how thick is the skin of a soap bubble?
80453.e: The skin of a soap bubble is wafer-thin. It is much thinner than a human hair.
80453.m: The skin of a soap bubble is wafer-thin.

80454.q: What do you mix to make a simple bubble mixture?
80454.e: For soap bubbles you need water and something soapy such as washing-up liquid. Together they make a stretchy skin.
80454.m: Water and washing-up liquid make a bubble mixture.

80455.e: Foam is made of lots of bubbles full of air. Between the bubbles are thin walls of liquid.
80455.m: Foam is made of lots of little air bubbles.

80456.q: Which foam do you get when you beat egg white hard?
80456.e: When beating, air is stirred into the egg white. It turns white and stiff and is then called whisked egg white.
80456.m: Beaten egg white is called whisked egg white.

80457.q: What do you whip to make whipped cream?
80457.e: When whipping, air gets into the cream. The fat in the cream holds the bubbles in place.
80457.m: Whipping cream turns it into whipped cream.

80458.q: What do firefighters often use to put out burning petrol?
80458.e: The foam lies over the burning petrol like a blanket. Then no more air can reach the fire.

a: It contains a lot of flour
80459.e: Each bubble reflects a little light in all directions. Together the many bubbles look white, much like snow.
80459.m: Lots of little bubbles make foam look white.

80460.q: Where can you find solid foam?
80460.e: Foam rubber is solid foam with lots of air bubbles. That is why a mattress is soft and light.
80460.m: Foam rubber is solid foam full of air.

80461.q: Which drink often has a layer of milk froth on top?
80461.e: For a cappuccino, milk is frothed up with hot steam. The froth goes on top of the coffee.
80461.m: A cappuccino has milk froth on top.

80462.q: What happens to foam if you wait a long time?
80462.e: The thin walls of the bubbles get thinner over time and burst. That is why foam slowly sinks down.

80463.q: Why do you put washing-up liquid in the washing-up water?
a: It loosens the grease from the dishes
80463.e: Grease sticks to dishes and is hard to wash off with water alone. Washing-up liquid loosens the grease so the water can rinse it away.
80463.m: Washing-up liquid loosens grease from dishes.

80464.q: What happens if you add a little washing-up liquid to milk with drops of colour?
80464.e: The washing-up liquid changes the surface of the milk and loosens the milk fat. This sets the colours moving.
80464.m: Washing-up liquid sets drops of colour on milk moving.

80465.q: Why must ordinary washing-up liquid not go into the dishwasher?
a: It makes far too much foam
80465.e: Washing-up liquid foams a lot. In the machine the foam would pour out, so it needs its own product.
80465.m: Only dishwasher detergent goes into the dishwasher.

80466.q: You drip water onto a coin. What changes if there is washing-up liquid in the water?
a: Many more drops fit on it
80466.e: Pure water forms a high dome on the coin. Washing-up liquid weakens the skin of the water, so it overflows sooner.
80466.m: With washing-up liquid, water does not form such a high dome.

80467.q: What must you never do with washing-up liquid?
80467.e: Washing-up liquid is for cleaning, not for eating or drinking. Keep it where small children cannot reach it.

80468.q: How much washing-up liquid do you need for a bowl of washing-up water?
80468.e: Washing-up liquid works even in small amounts. Too much is unnecessary and pollutes the waste water.
80468.m: A few squirts of washing-up liquid are enough for the washing-up.

80469.q: Why should you put cream on your hands after a long time washing up?
a: Washing-up liquid dries out the skin
Washing-up liquid makes the skin hot
Washing-up liquid makes the skin thick
80469.e: Washing-up liquid removes not only grease from dishes but also the skin's natural oils. A cream gives the skin back its oils.
80469.m: Washing-up liquid can dry out the skin.

80471.q: What happens when you shake a bottle of oil and water hard?
80471.e: When shaken, the oil breaks up into lots of tiny droplets that float in the water. The liquid then looks cloudy.
80471.m: When shaken, oil in water breaks up into tiny droplets.

80472.q: What must you never use to put out burning oil in a pan?
80472.e: Water sinks under the hot oil, turns to steam at once and throws burning oil out. It is better to smother the fire with a lid.
80472.m: Never put out burning oil with water.

80473.q: Which sauce is made from oil and egg yolk that mix well?
80473.e: Egg yolk contains a substance that joins oil and water. That is why oil and egg yolk become a thick mayonnaise.
80473.m: Mayonnaise is a mixture of oil and egg yolk.

80474.q: In which drink are tiny droplets of fat spread through water?
80474.e: Milk is mostly water. Tiny droplets of fat float in it, which is why it is white and not see-through.
80474.m: Tiny droplets of fat float in milk.

80475.q: What do you call a mixture of tiny oil droplets in water?
80475.e: An emulsion is a mixture of two liquids that do not normally mix. One floats in tiny droplets in the other.
80475.m: A mixture of oil droplets in water is called an emulsion.

80476.q: What helps oil and water mix better?
80476.e: Washing-up liquid can cling to oil and to water at the same time. In this way it joins the two liquids.
80476.m: Washing-up liquid helps oil and water mix.

80477.q: Why can't you wash an oil stain out of a jumper with water alone?
a: Oil is too cold for it
80477.e: Water simply runs off the oil in beads. You need soap or detergent to loosen the oil.
80477.m: Wash oil stains with soap, not just with water.

80478.q: What do you do with a salad dressing of oil and vinegar just before serving?
80478.e: Oil and vinegar separate when the dressing stands. Shaking or stirring mixes them again.
80478.m: Shake a salad dressing well before serving.

80479.q: What makes the lumps of wax in a lava lamp rise?
80479.e: At the bottom of the lava lamp is a light bulb. It warms the wax, which expands, gets lighter and rises.
80479.m: In a lava lamp, heat makes the wax rise.

80480.q: What happens to the wax at the top of a lava lamp?
80480.e: It is cooler at the top than at the bottom. The wax cools, becomes heavier again and sinks back down.
80480.m: Cooled wax sinks down in a lava lamp.

80481.q: What do you see in a lava lamp?
a: Coloured blobs floating up and down
80481.e: In a lava lamp, soft, coloured blobs of wax float slowly upwards and back down again.
80481.m: In a lava lamp, blobs of wax float up and down.

80482.q: What makes the bubbles rise in a home-made lava lamp of water and oil?
80482.e: The effervescent tablet fizzes in the water and forms gas bubbles. These carry coloured drops of water upwards.
80482.m: An effervescent tablet makes a home-made lava lamp bubble.

80483.q: What does the food colouring colour in a home-made lava lamp of water and oil?
80483.e: Food colouring dissolves in water but not in oil. That is why the oil stays clear and only the water becomes coloured.
80483.m: Food colouring colours water but not oil.

80484.q: Why does it take a while for a real lava lamp to start bubbling after it is switched on?
a: The wax has to warm up first
The water has to freeze first
The lamp has to dry first
80484.e: At first the wax is solid and cold. Only when it is warm and soft do the blobs start to rise.
80484.m: A lava lamp needs time for the wax to warm up.

80485.q: Why should you not shake a warm lava lamp?
80485.e: When shaken, wax and liquid mix into tiny droplets. The lamp can then stay cloudy for a long time.
80485.m: Never shake a warm lava lamp.

80486.q: Where does the lava lamp get its name from?
a: It is filled with real lava
It was invented on a volcano
It gets as hot as lava
80486.e: The slowly flowing blobs of wax look like glowing lava from a volcano. That is why it is called a lava lamp.
80486.m: The wax blobs in a lava lamp look like lava.

80487.q: What can you easily use to grow crystals at home?
80487.e: You dissolve a lot of salt or sugar in water. As the water slowly evaporates, crystals grow from it.
80487.m: You can grow crystals from salt water or sugar water.

80488.q: Why do you dissolve the salt in warm water to grow crystals?
a: The salt turns colourful in it
The salt turns sweet in it
The salt goes hard in it
80488.e: Warm water can take up more salt than cold. The more salt is dissolved, the better the crystals grow.
80488.m: More salt dissolves in warm water.

80489.q: What do you hang in the salt solution so that crystals grow on it?
80489.e: You tie a piece of string to a pencil and lay the pencil across the glass. The crystals form on the string.
80489.m: Crystals grow on a string in the salt solution.

80490.q: How long does it take for nice crystals to grow?
80490.e: Crystals grow slowly while the water evaporates. So you need patience and should check every day.
80490.m: Growing crystals takes several days of patience.

80491.q: Where is the best place to put the glass with the crystal solution?
80491.e: Crystals grow best when the glass is not moved. Shaking disturbs their growth.
80491.m: Crystals grow best in a quiet place.

80492.q: What are the large sugar crystals you can put in tea called?
80492.e: Rock sugar forms when sugar slowly crystallises out of a solution. This produces large, clear crystals.
80492.m: Rock sugar is made of large sugar crystals.

80493.q: How many arms does a snow crystal have?
80493.e: Snow crystals are ice crystals. Because of the way ice is built, snowflakes have six arms or six points.
80493.m: A snow crystal has six arms.

80495.q: What is rock crystal made of?
80495.e: Rock crystal is clear, transparent quartz. Especially beautiful pieces are found in the Swiss Alps.
80495.m: Rock crystal is made of quartz.

80496.q: What colour is table salt in the tub?
80496.e: A single pure salt crystal is actually transparent. Lots of small grains together look white.

80497.q: Why did people in the past put meat and fish in salt?
80497.e: Salt draws water out of food. Without water, bacteria can hardly multiply, so salted food goes off less quickly.
80497.m: Salt makes meat and fish keep longer.

80498.q: Which animals like to lick a salt lick in the barn?
80498.e: Cows need salt, but they find too little of it in grass. That is why they get a salt lick in the barn or in the field.
80498.m: Cows like to lick a salt lick.

80499.q: Which bake is often sprinkled with coarse grains of salt?
80499.e: Pretzels are sprinkled with coarse salt before baking. The other bakes are usually sweet or have no salt crust.
80499.m: Pretzels are sprinkled with coarse salt.

80500.q: What is salt that is mined deep in the earth called?
80500.e: A very long time ago, seas dried up and left layers of salt behind. This salt in the ground is called rock salt.
80500.m: Salt from the earth is called rock salt.

80501.q: What do you use to sprinkle salt on your food at the table?
80501.e: A salt cellar has little holes at the top. That way only a little salt lands on the food.
80501.m: You season food at the table with a salt cellar.

80502.q: How much salt should you use with your food?
80502.e: The body needs some salt. But too much salt is unhealthy, so use it sparingly.

80601.q: The PostBus leaves at 8.10 and arrives in the village at 8.30. How long does the journey take?
80601.m: The journey time is the time between departure and arrival.

80602.q: A train runs every half hour. One leaves at 9.00. When does the next one leave?
80602.e: Half an hour has 30 minutes. 9.00 plus 30 minutes is 9.30.

80603.q: The timetable says 14.00. What time is that in the afternoon?
80603.e: After 12 o’clock you keep counting: 13, 14 and so on. 14 − 12 = 2, so it is 2 o’clock in the afternoon.
80603.m: Timetables count the hours up to 24.

80604.q: The tram runs every 10 minutes. One leaves at 7.20. When does the next one leave?
80604.m: With a regular timetable, the trams always run at the same interval.

80605.q: You are at the bus stop at 10.05. The next bus leaves at 10.20. How long do you wait?
80605.m: You work out the waiting time from now until departure.

80606.q: A train leaves at 17.50. The journey takes 20 minutes. When does it arrive?
80606.e: It is 10 minutes until 18.00, then another 10 minutes. So the train arrives at 18.10.
80606.m: After 59 minutes a new hour begins.

80607.q: What is the place called where a bus or tram stops so that you can get on?
80607.e: The bus or tram stops at the stop. The timetable often hangs there too.
80607.m: You get on the bus at the bus stop.

80608.q: Which departure in the timetable is the earliest?
80608.e: 6 o’clock comes before 7 and 8 o’clock. So 6.45 is the earliest departure.
80608.m: First compare the hours, then the minutes.

80609.q: A bus leaves every hour on the hour, from 6 o’clock up to and including 9 o’clock. How many departures is that?
80609.e: The bus leaves at 6, 7, 8 and 9 o’clock. That is 4 departures.
80609.m: When counting departures, you count the first and the last.

80610.q: You need 2 eggs for a cake. You bake 2 cakes. How many eggs do you need?
80610.e: For 2 cakes you need twice as many eggs: 2 + 2 = 4.
80610.m: Doubling means taking a number twice.

80611.q: The recipe says 200 g of flour. You double the recipe. How much flour do you need?
80611.e: Twice 200 g is 200 g + 200 g = 400 g.
80611.m: When doubling, you take every ingredient twice.

80612.q: A recipe for 4 people needs 1 litre of milk. How much milk do you need for 8 people?
80612.e: 8 people is twice as many as 4 people. So you need twice as much milk, which is 2 litres.
80612.m: For twice as many people you need twice as much.

80613.q: What does “g” mean in “100 g sugar” in a recipe?
80613.e: The letter g stands for grams. Grams measure how heavy something is.
80613.m: A gram is a measure of weight.

80614.q: The recipe says 3 tablespoons of sugar. You double the recipe. How many tablespoons do you need?
80614.e: 3 + 3 = 6. So you need 6 tablespoons of sugar.

80615.q: A recipe for 6 people needs 600 g of pasta. How much do you need for 3 people?
80615.e: 3 people is half of 6 people. Half of 600 g is 300 g.
80615.m: For half as many people you need half as much.

80616.q: The recipe says “1 tsp salt”. What does “tsp” stand for?
80616.e: Tsp is short for teaspoon. A tablespoon is written tbsp in recipes.
80616.m: In recipes, tsp means teaspoon and tbsp means tablespoon.

80617.q: The recipe says 250 g of butter. You double the recipe. How much butter do you need?

80618.q: The receipt says: bread 3 francs, milk 2 francs. What is the total?
80618.m: The total is the sum of all the prices.

80619.q: Your shopping costs 7 francs. You pay with 10 francs. How much change do you get?
80619.m: The change is the money you paid minus the price.

80620.q: What is the amount at the very bottom of the receipt called, which adds everything up?
80620.e: The total is at the bottom of the receipt. That is how much you have to pay for everything together.
80620.m: The total shows how much everything costs together.

80621.q: A yoghurt costs 1 franc 50 and an apple 50 centimes. How much do they cost together?
80621.e: 50 centimes + 50 centimes is 1 franc. Add 1 franc and it makes 2 francs.
80621.m: Two lots of 50 centimes make one franc.

80622.q: You buy 3 bread rolls. Each costs 1 franc. What does the receipt say?
80622.m: For identical things at the same price, you can multiply.

80623.q: The total is 15 francs. You pay with a 20-franc note. How much change do you get?
80623.m: For the change, you subtract the price from the money you paid.

80624.q: What do you get at the checkout that lists all your shopping?
80624.e: The receipt shows all the things you bought with their prices.
80624.m: The receipt lists all your shopping with prices.

80625.q: The total is 8 francs 40. You pay with 10 francs. How much change do you get?
80625.e: From 8 francs 40 to 9 francs is 60 centimes, and to 10 francs another 1 franc. Together that is 1 franc 60.
80625.m: For change, you can count up from the price to the amount paid.

80626.q: The receipt says: 2 croissants, 1 franc 50 each. How much do the croissants cost together?
80626.m: Two lots of 1 franc 50 make three francs.

80627.q: Entry for a child costs 5 francs. How much do 2 children pay?
80627.m: For several people, you multiply the entry price by the number of people.

80628.q: Adults pay 12 francs entry, children 6 francs. How much do 1 adult and 1 child pay?
80628.m: You add different entry prices together.

80629.q: At the museum, children under 6 get in free. How much does a 4-year-old child pay?
80629.e: 4 years is younger than 6 years. So entry is free, which means 0 francs.

80630.q: At the swimming pool, entry for a child costs 3 francs. How much do 4 children pay?

80631.q: Adults pay 10 francs, children 5 francs. How much do 2 adults and 2 children pay?
80631.e: 2 adults pay 20 francs, 2 children pay 10 francs. 20 + 10 = 30 francs.
80631.m: First work out each group, then add them together.

80632.q: Single tickets for a family cost 28 francs. The family ticket costs 22 francs. How much does the family save?
80632.e: 28 − 22 = 6. With the family ticket, the family saves 6 francs.
80632.m: The saving is the difference between two prices.

80633.q: The zoo costs 8 francs for children. You have 10 francs. How much money do you have left?
80633.m: You work out what is left with subtraction.

80634.q: A cinema ticket costs 15 francs. How much do 3 tickets cost?

80635.q: There are 5 francs in your piggy bank. You put in 2 francs more. How much is in it now?
80635.e: 5 + 2 = 7. Now there are 7 francs in the piggy bank.
80635.m: When you put money in, you add.

80636.q: You put 1 franc in your piggy bank every week. How much have you saved after 4 weeks?
80636.m: If you save regularly, you add a little every week.

80637.q: In the piggy bank there are three 1-franc coins and one 2-franc coin. How much money is that?
80637.m: When counting money, the value of the coins counts, not how many there are.

80638.q: You want a ball for 12 francs. You have 8 francs in your piggy bank. How much more do you need?
80638.m: What you still need is the price minus the money saved.

80639.q: You save 2 francs every week. After how many weeks do you have 10 francs?

80640.q: In the piggy bank there are five 20-centime coins. How much money is that?
80640.e: 5 times 20 centimes is 100 centimes. 100 centimes is 1 franc.

80641.q: For 3 weeks you put 5 francs in your piggy bank every week. How much have you saved then?

80642.q: There are 20 francs in the piggy bank. You take out 6 francs. How much is left in it?
80642.e: 20 − 6 = 14. There are 14 francs left in the piggy bank.
80642.m: When you take money out, you subtract.

80643.q: An apple costs 60 centimes in shop A and 80 centimes in shop B. Where is the apple cheaper?
80643.e: 60 centimes is less than 80 centimes. So the apple is cheaper in shop A.
80643.m: The cheaper shop is the one with the lower price.

80644.e: First you compare the francs: 3 is more than 2. With the same francs, 50 centimes is the most.
80644.m: With prices, you compare the francs first and then the centimes.

80645.q: An exercise book costs 2 francs. A pack of 3 costs 5 francs. How much do you save with the pack of 3?
80645.e: 3 single exercise books cost 3 times 2 = 6 francs. 6 − 5 = 1, so you save 1 franc.
80645.m: A pack is worth it if it costs less than the single items.

80646.q: A game costs 9 francs in the shop and 6 francs online. How much more expensive is it in the shop?
80646.e: 9 − 6 = 3. The game is 3 francs more expensive in the shop.
80646.m: You work out a price difference with subtraction.

80647.q: A bike costs 200 francs. In the sale it costs only 150 francs. How much cheaper is it?
80647.m: In a sale, lots of things are cheaper than usual.

80648.e: All the prices have 1 franc. Of the centimes, 9 is the least.
80648.m: When the francs are the same, the centimes decide.

80649.q: What does “special offer” mean on a price label in a shop?
a: It is more expensive than usual
80649.e: With a special offer, the shop sells something more cheaply for a short time. That way you can save money.
80649.m: A special offer is a deal at a lower price.

80650.q: Lena has 5 francs. Which book can she buy?
80650.e: Only 4 francs 80 is less than 5 francs. All the other books are more expensive.
80650.m: You can only buy what costs at most as much as you have.

80651.q: On one side of a street, the house numbers are 2, 4, 6. Which number comes next?
80651.e: This side has even numbers. After 6 comes the even number 8.
80651.m: Often one side of a street has even numbers and the other odd numbers.

80652.q: On one side of a street, the house numbers are 1, 3, 5. Which number comes next?
80652.e: These are odd numbers; you always add 2. 5 + 2 = 7.

80653.q: Which house number is an even number?
80653.e: 12 ends in 2 and can be divided by 2. So 12 is even.

80654.q: House number 9 has a neighbouring house on the left and right on the same side of the street. What numbers do the neighbouring houses have?
80654.e: On a side of the street with odd numbers, you count in twos. Before 9 comes 7, after 9 comes 11.
80654.m: Neighbouring houses on the same side usually differ by two.

80655.q: You walk along a street and see the house numbers 20, 18, 16. Which comes next?
80655.e: The numbers get 2 smaller each time. 16 − 2 = 14.
80655.m: Counting backwards in twos, you always take away 2.

80656.q: How many houses are there on the same side of the street between house number 2 and house number 10?
80656.e: In between are houses 4, 6 and 8. That is 3 houses.
80656.m: Between two numbers, you do not count the two end numbers.

80657.q: Which house number is the largest?
80657.e: All the numbers have three digits. 210 has 2 hundreds and 1 ten, which is the most.
80657.m: With big numbers, you compare the hundreds first.

80658.q: Lea lives at house number 23. How many tens does this number have?
80658.e: 23 is made up of 2 tens and 3 ones.
80658.m: In a two-digit number, the number of tens is at the front.

80659.q: In a Swiss address, what comes right after the street name?
80659.e: In Switzerland you write, for example, “Bahnhofstrasse 12”. The house number follows the street name.
80659.m: The house number comes after the street name.

80660.q: What colour are the hiking signposts in Switzerland?
80660.e: In Switzerland, the signposts for hiking trails are yellow. They are easy to see in nature.

80661.q: A hiking signpost says “Hut 2 h”. What does the “h” mean?
80661.e: The “h” stands for hours. So it takes about 2 hours to hike to the hut.
80661.m: On signposts, h stands for hours and min for minutes.

80662.q: The signpost shows: lake 45 min, village 1 h 15 min. How much longer do you hike to the village?
80662.m: One hour and 15 minutes is 75 minutes.

80663.q: The signpost says “1 h 30 min”. How many minutes is that?
80663.m: An hour and a half is 90 minutes.

80664.q: What colours mark a mountain hiking trail in Switzerland?
80664.e: Mountain hiking trails are marked white-red-white. They are steeper and harder than yellow hiking trails.
80664.m: You can recognise mountain hiking trails by the white-red-white marking.

80665.q: The signpost shows 20 min to the viewpoint. You go there and take just as long to come back. How long do you hike?
80665.e: It is 20 minutes there and another 20 minutes back. 20 + 20 = 40 minutes.
80665.m: For the way there and back, you add both times together.

80666.q: You set off at 10 o’clock. The signpost shows “Summit 2 h”. Roughly when will you be at the top?
80666.m: The arrival time is the start time plus the hiking time.

80667.q: What is written next to the destination on a Swiss hiking signpost?
80667.e: Next to each destination it says roughly how long it takes to hike there. That way you can plan the hike.
80667.m: Hiking signposts show the time to the destination.

80668.q: Lisa’s birthday is on 5 May, Tim’s on 12 May. Whose birthday comes first?
80668.e: Both have their birthday in May. The 5th comes before the 12th, so Lisa celebrates first.
80668.m: In the same month, the smaller day comes first.

80669.e: The months go like this: January, February, March, April. After March comes April.
80669.m: April is the fourth month of the year.

80670.q: Today is 3 June. Your birthday is on 10 June. How many more days is it?
80670.e: 10 − 3 = 7. It is 7 more days, which is exactly one week.

80671.q: Today is Monday. Your birthday is in 2 days. Which day of the week is it on?
80671.e: After Monday comes Tuesday, then Wednesday. So in 2 days it is Wednesday.
80671.m: The days of the week always follow in the same order.

80672.q: Which month is the last in the year?
80672.e: December is the 12th and last month. After that, a new year begins with January.

80673.q: Mia turns 7 today. How old will she be on her next birthday?
80673.e: On every birthday you get one year older. 7 + 1 = 8.
80673.m: On every birthday you get one year older.

80674.q: Ben’s birthday is in February, Ana’s in October and Leo’s in July. Who celebrates first in the year?
80674.e: February comes before July and October. So Ben celebrates first.
80674.m: The order of the months shows who celebrates first.

80676.q: On Monday you have 4 lessons in the morning and 2 lessons in the afternoon. How many lessons is that altogether?
80676.m: You add morning and afternoon lessons together.

80677.q: The timetable shows 2 PE lessons one after the other. Each lasts 45 minutes. How long do you do PE?
80677.e: 45 + 45 = 90 minutes. That is an hour and a half.
80677.m: Two lessons one after the other are called a double lesson.

80678.q: According to the timetable you have PE every Tuesday and every Friday. How many times do you have PE in 2 weeks?
80678.e: In one week you have PE twice. In 2 weeks it is 2 + 2 = 4 times.
80678.m: What is the same every week can be added up for several weeks.

80679.q: School starts at 8.00. The first lesson lasts 45 minutes. When does it finish?
80679.m: The end is the start plus the length of time.

80680.q: On how many days a week do you normally have school?
80680.e: School is from Monday to Friday. That is 5 days; Saturday and Sunday are free.
80680.m: A school week has five school days.

80681.q: Break lasts from 10.00 to 10.20. How long is break?
80681.m: The length of time is the time from the start to the end.

80682.q: On which afternoon do many Swiss primary schools have no school?
80682.e: In many Swiss schools, Wednesday afternoon is free. Then many children have time for sport or music.
80682.m: Wednesday afternoon is free in many schools.

80683.q: The timetable has 5 maths lessons and 1 music lesson a week. How many more maths lessons are there?
80683.m: You work out the difference between two numbers with subtraction.

80684.q: A football match ends 3:1. How many goals were scored altogether?
80684.e: One team scored 3 goals, the other 1. 3 + 1 = 4 goals.
80684.m: You add up all the goals together.

80685.q: A team wins 5:2. By how many goals did it win?
80685.m: You work out the goal difference with subtraction.

80686.q: A match ends 1:1. What is this result called?
80686.e: Both teams scored the same number of goals. Nobody won, so it is called a draw.
80686.m: If both teams score the same number of goals, the match is a draw.

80687.q: How many points does a football team get for a win in the league?
80687.e: In football leagues, a win earns 3 points. A defeat earns no points.
80687.m: A win in football brings three points.

80688.q: How many points does a football team get for a draw in the league?
80688.e: In a draw, both teams get 1 point each.
80688.m: A draw brings each team one point.

80689.q: A football team has 2 wins and 1 draw. A win gives 3 points, a draw 1 point. How many points does it have?
80689.e: 2 wins give 3 + 3 = 6 points. The draw adds 1 point: 6 + 1 = 7.
80689.m: You add up the points from all the matches.

80690.q: Which medal does the winner of a ski race get for 1st place?
80690.e: 1st place gets gold, 2nd place silver and 3rd place bronze.
80690.m: First place gets a gold medal.

80691.q: In the long jump, Anna jumps 3 m, Ben 2 m 80 cm and Cem 3 m 10 cm. Who wins?
80691.e: 3 m 10 cm is the furthest. So Cem wins.
80691.m: In the long jump, whoever jumps furthest wins.

80692.q: The stopwatch shows 45 seconds. How many seconds are left until a whole minute?
80692.e: A whole minute has 60 seconds. 60 − 45 = 15 seconds.
80692.m: To reach the full minute, you work from 60 seconds.

80693.q: In a race, Lea runs in 12 seconds and Tim in 14 seconds. Who was faster?
80693.e: Lea took less time than Tim. Whoever takes less time is faster.
80693.m: The shorter the time, the faster you were.

80694.q: The stopwatch shows 1 minute and 10 seconds. How many seconds is that?
80694.m: You convert minutes into seconds by multiplying by 60.

80695.q: Why do you press “Start” on a stopwatch?
a: So that the watch gets quieter
So that the time is deleted
80695.e: With Start, the stopwatch begins to count. With Stop it stops and shows the measured time.
80695.m: A stopwatch measures how long something takes.

80696.q: Tim takes 20 seconds, Mia 25 seconds. By how many seconds was Tim faster?
80696.m: You work out the time difference with subtraction.

80698.q: Who wins a race timed with a stopwatch?
a: Whoever has the biggest start number
80698.e: The winner is whoever completes the course fastest. That is the shortest measured time.
80698.m: In a race, the shortest time wins.

80699.q: How many seconds are half a minute?
80699.e: A minute has 60 seconds. Half of 60 is 30.
80699.m: Half a minute has thirty seconds.

80700.q: You run 3 laps. Each lap takes 10 seconds. How long do you run altogether?
80700.m: Three times ten seconds makes thirty seconds.

80701.e: A command says what someone should do. “Go!” tells you to set off.
80701.m: A command says exactly what to do.

80702.q: A robot only knows a few commands. What happens if you give it a command it does not know?
80702.e: A robot can only carry out the commands it knows. It does not understand anything else.
80702.m: A robot only carries out commands it knows.

80703.q: Why does a command for a robot have to be completely exact?
a: Because it does not think for itself
Because it likes reading for a long time
80703.e: A robot does exactly what the command says. It cannot guess what you really mean.
80703.m: A robot does exactly what you tell it.

80704.q: Which command fits to make a game character hop?
80704.e: Jumping and hopping mean almost the same thing. That is why the command “Jump!” fits.
80704.m: Each command triggers a particular action.

80705.q: With which command does a robot move back without turning round?
80705.e: With the command backwards, the robot moves back. It keeps facing the same way while doing so.

80706.q: The command is: “Clap twice, then stamp once.” How many movements do you make?
80706.e: Clapping twice and stamping once makes 2 + 1 = 3 movements together.
80706.m: You carry out every part of a command.

80707.q: What does the command “Save” do on the computer?
80707.e: When saving, the computer stores your work. That way you can open it again later.
80707.m: If you save, you do not lose your work.

80708.q: The teacher says: “Stand up, take your exercise book, sit down.” How many commands is that?
80708.e: Standing up, taking the exercise book and sitting down are three commands.
80708.m: Several commands one after the other make a set of instructions.

80709.q: With which command does a robot face left without moving away?
80709.e: When turning, the robot stays in its place. Afterwards it faces a different direction.
80709.m: When turning, the robot stays in the same place.

80710.q: Which order is right when washing your hands?
a: Wet them, soap them, rinse them
Soap them, rinse them, wet them
Rinse them, wet them, soap them
Soap them, wet them, dry them
80710.e: First you wet your hands, then you soap them and rinse the soap off.
80710.m: In a set of instructions, the order matters.

80711.q: A robot should first move 2 squares forwards and then turn right. What happens if it turns first?
a: It goes in a different direction
It arrives in the same place
80711.e: If it turns first, it is already facing right. Then it moves the 2 squares in that direction and ends up somewhere else.
80711.m: Swapped commands often lead to a different destination.

80712.q: You are making a slice of bread and butter. What comes first?
80712.e: You cannot spread butter without bread. That is why you take the slice of bread first.
80712.m: Some steps only work once another one is finished.

80713.q: You want to ride your bike. What do you do first?
80713.e: You put your helmet on before riding off. That way your head is protected from the start.
80713.m: You put on your helmet before cycling.

80714.q: Which order is right when planting?
a: Dig a hole, put the seed in, water
Water, dig a hole, put the seed in
Put the seed in, dig a hole, water
Water, put the seed in, dig a hole
80714.e: First you need a hole. Then the seed goes in, and finally you water it.
80714.m: Every set of instructions has a sensible order.

80715.q: A program has the commands A, B and C. In which order does the computer carry them out?
80715.e: A computer carries out the commands one after the other, from the first to the last.
80715.m: A computer works through commands in order.

80716.q: You are sending a letter. What do you do last?
80716.e: Only when the letter is finished, addressed and stamped do you put it in the postbox.
80716.m: The last step only comes when everything else is done.

80717.q: What do you call the sequence “first, then, after that, finally”?
80717.e: With these words you describe what happens one after the other. That is an order.
80717.m: The order says what comes first and what comes after.

80718.q: You are baking a cake. What comes last?
a: Taking the cake out of the oven
Pouring the batter into the tin
80718.e: First you mix the batter and pour it into the tin. Right at the end you take the finished cake out of the oven.
80718.m: When baking, one step follows another.

80719.q: How can you say “forwards, forwards, forwards” more briefly?
80719.e: The same command appears three times. That is why you can say: 3 times forwards.
80719.m: You can combine the same commands with a repetition.

80720.q: A robot drives a square with “1 square forwards, turn right”. How many times do you have to repeat this?
80720.e: A square has 4 sides and 4 corners. That is why you repeat the commands 4 times.
80720.m: For a square you repeat four identical parts.

80721.q: Repeat 4 times: put a block on the tower. The tower was empty before. How many blocks does the tower have afterwards?
80721.e: With each repetition, 1 block is added. After 4 repetitions, 4 blocks are stacked on top of each other.
80721.m: Each repetition carries out the command once.

80722.q: Repeat 3 times: 2 steps forwards. How many steps do you take?

80723.q: Why do people use repetitions when programming?
80723.e: Instead of writing the same command many times, you write it once with a number. That keeps the program short and clear.

80724.q: Repeat 3 times: paint red, paint yellow. Which colour do you paint last?
80724.e: Each repetition ends with yellow. That is why the last colour is yellow.
80724.m: A repetition always ends with its last command.

80725.q: A song has a chorus that comes again and again. What is something like this called in computer science?
80725.e: The chorus is sung several times. In computer science this is called a repetition.
80725.m: Something that happens the same way several times is a repetition.

80726.q: Repeat 5 times: stamp. After that you clap once. How many movements is that?
80726.e: Stamping 5 times and clapping once gives 5 + 1 = 6 movements.
80726.m: You add on commands that come after a repetition.

80727.q: What does the educational robot Bee-Bot look like?
80727.e: As its name says, the Bee-Bot is a bee. It has yellow and black stripes like a bee.
80727.m: The Bee-Bot is a robot shaped like a bee.

80728.q: Which button makes the Bee-Bot start its commands?
80728.e: The green GO button starts the program. Then the Bee-Bot carries out all the commands in order.
80728.m: On the Bee-Bot, the GO button starts the program.

80729.q: How far does the Bee-Bot turn if you press the right arrow once?
80729.e: The Bee-Bot turns 90 degrees with each turn command. That is a quarter turn.
80729.m: The Bee-Bot always turns a quarter turn.

80730.q: What does the button with the X do on the Bee-Bot?
80730.e: With the X button you clear all the stored steps. Then you can enter a new program.
80730.m: Before a new program, you clear the old commands.

80731.q: What happens if you do not clear the Bee-Bot before entering new commands?
a: It carries out the old commands too
It does not move at all
It only carries out the last command
80731.e: The Bee-Bot remembers the old commands. The new ones are added at the end, and it takes a completely different route.
80731.m: Old commands stay stored until you clear them.

80732.q: How far does the Bee-Bot move with a single forwards command?
80732.e: With each forwards command, the Bee-Bot moves a short distance of about 15 centimetres. That is about as long as a school ruler.
80732.m: One Bee-Bot step is about 15 centimetres long.

80733.q: What does the Bee-Bot do with a pause command?
80733.e: With a pause, the Bee-Bot stands still for about one second. Then it carries on with the next command.
80733.m: A pause makes the robot wait briefly.

80734.q: What does the Bee-Bot usually move on in the classroom?
80734.e: The squares of the mat match exactly one Bee-Bot step. That way you can count the steps easily.
80734.m: On a mat with squares you can plan routes well.

80735.q: What does an Ozobot follow when it moves on paper?
80735.e: The Ozobot recognises lines on the paper and follows them. That way you can draw a route for it.

80736.q: Which pen colours do you need for the Ozobot's codes?
80736.e: The Ozobot recognises black lines as well as red, green and blue colour patches. You write its codes with these colours.
80736.m: Ozobot codes are made of red, green, blue and black.

80737.q: What is a colour code for the Ozobot?
a: A sequence of colour patches on the line
A song to sing along to
80737.e: On the line you colour short sections in different colours one after the other. When the Ozobot moves over them, it reads the code.
80737.m: Colour codes are commands for the Ozobot.

80738.q: What can a colour code tell the Ozobot to do?
80738.e: Colour codes can, for example, make the Ozobot go faster or slower or turn.
80738.m: With colour codes you change how the Ozobot moves.

80739.q: Where does the Ozobot have the sensors it uses to recognise lines?
80739.e: The sensors look down at the paper. That way the Ozobot sees the line and the colours underneath it.
80739.m: The Ozobot reads lines with sensors on its underside.

80740.q: How can you also program an Ozobot without drawn lines?
80740.e: With the program OzoBlockly you put blocks together into a program. This is then loaded onto the Ozobot.
80740.m: You can also program Ozobots with blocks.

80741.q: What does an Ozobot do at a junction without a colour code?
a: It chooses a path at random
80741.e: Without a colour code, the Ozobot does not know where to go. That is why it decides at random.
80741.m: A colour code before the junction tells the Ozobot where to go.

80742.e: The Ozobot is a small educational robot. With it, children learn how to give commands.
80742.m: The Ozobot is a small educational robot.

80743.q: Which age is the app ScratchJr mainly intended for?
80743.e: ScratchJr was made for children aged 5 to 7. They can use it to program even if they cannot read well yet.
80743.m: ScratchJr is a programming app for young children.

80744.q: In which direction do you put the blocks together in ScratchJr?
80744.e: In ScratchJr, the blocks are lined up like words in a sentence, from left to right.
80744.m: In ScratchJr you read a program from left to right.

80745.q: What do you often start a program with in ScratchJr?
80745.e: A program often begins with the green flag block. If you tap the green flag, all these programs start running.
80745.m: The green flag starts programs in ScratchJr.

80746.q: Which character is already there when you start a new project in ScratchJr?
80746.e: The cat is the well-known character of Scratch and ScratchJr. It is ready in every new project.
80746.m: In ScratchJr you start with the cat.

a: Younger children from about 5 years old
80747.e: ScratchJr is a simpler version of Scratch. Children who can hardly read yet use it to put picture blocks together on a tablet.
80747.m: ScratchJr is a tablet app for younger children.

80748.q: What do the blue motion blocks do in ScratchJr?
80748.e: With the motion blocks, the character walks, jumps or turns.
80748.m: Motion blocks make the character walk and jump.

80749.q: What can you create yourself with ScratchJr?
80749.e: In ScratchJr you program characters and backgrounds. This creates your own stories and small games.
80749.m: With ScratchJr you invent your own stories and games.

80750.q: How much does the ScratchJr app cost?
80750.e: You can download ScratchJr for free. That way all children can learn with it.

80751.q: A robot is supposed to drive to the apple but drives into the wall. What is probably the reason?
a: There is a mistake in the program
80751.e: The robot does exactly what is in the program. If it goes the wrong way, a command is wrong or missing.
80751.m: If a robot goes the wrong way, look for the mistake in the program.

80752.q: Your program does not work. What do you do first?
a: Check the commands step by step
80752.e: If you look at each command one at a time, you find the mistake fastest.
80752.m: You find mistakes by checking step by step.

80753.q: A robot is supposed to move 3 squares forwards but moves 4. What is wrong?
80753.e: For 3 squares you need 3 forwards commands. If it moves 4 squares, there is one command too many in the program.
80753.m: Each square needs exactly one forwards command.

80754.q: A robot is supposed to turn right but turns left. How do you fix the mistake?
a: Replace turn left with turn right
80754.e: The wrong command is “turn left”. If you replace it with “turn right”, the route is correct.
80754.m: You replace a wrong command with the right one.

80755.q: Are mistakes in programming a bad thing?
a: No, you can find and fix them
80755.e: Everyone makes mistakes, even professionals. You look for them, correct them and learn as you go.
80755.m: You can learn from mistakes in programs.

80756.q: You want “clap, clap, hop”. The program says “clap, hop, clap”. What do you have to change?
80756.e: They are the right commands in the right number. Only the order is wrong.
80756.m: Sometimes the commands are right but not their order.

80757.q: How can you tell that a program has a mistake?
a: It does not do what it should
80757.e: A program is meant to do a task. If that does not work, there is a mistake in it.
80757.m: A mistake shows when a program does not work properly.

80758.q: A robot is supposed to move 2 squares forwards but stops after 1 square. What is missing?
80758.e: It only moves 1 square, so there is only 1 forwards command in the program. A second one is missing.
80758.m: If a command is missing, the robot stops too early.

80759.q: You enter commands into a robot but do not press start. What happens?
80759.e: A program only runs once you start it. Without starting, the robot stays still.
80759.m: A program only runs after you start it.

80760.q: Which symbol can often be seen on a start button?
80760.e: The triangle pointing right means start or play. You also know it from music and videos.
80760.m: The triangle pointing right means start.

80761.q: What does a filled-in square on a button usually mean?
80761.e: The square stands for stop. You use it to stop a program, music or a video.

80762.q: Which command does a program begin with?
80762.e: After starting, the computer first carries out the first command. Then the others follow in order.
80762.m: A program always begins with the first command.

80763.q: What must be switched on on an educational robot before a program can start?
80763.e: Only when the robot is switched on does it have power. Then it can accept and carry out commands.
80763.m: A robot needs power to work.

80764.q: Where do you put the robot before starting the program?
80764.e: The program is planned for a route from the start square. If the robot is somewhere else, it does not reach the finish.
80764.m: Before starting, you put the robot on the start square.

80765.q: What does a symbol with two vertical lines on a button mean?
80765.e: Two vertical lines stand for pause. Afterwards it can carry on from the same place.

80766.q: Why is it important which way the robot is facing at the start?
a: Because all the commands depend on it
Because otherwise it does not light up
Because otherwise it does not beep
80766.e: Forwards always means the way it is facing. If it faces the wrong way at the start, it takes the whole route wrongly.
80766.m: The direction it faces at the start decides the whole route.

80767.q: Which way does the arrow ↑ point?
80767.e: The tip of the arrow shows the direction. With ↑ it points up.
80767.m: The arrow's tip shows the direction.

80768.q: Which way does the arrow ← point?
80768.e: The tip of the arrow ← points to the left.
80768.m: An arrow points in the direction of its tip.

80769.q: Which arrow points to the right?
80769.e: With the arrow →, the tip points to the right.
80769.m: The arrow to the right has its tip on the right.

80770.e: With the arrow ↓, the tip points down.
80770.m: The arrow pointing down has its tip at the bottom.

80771.q: A game board shows the arrows ↑ ↑ →. Each arrow means 1 square. How many squares do you go up?
80771.e: Two arrows point up. That is why you go 2 squares up.
80771.m: You add up arrows that are the same.

80772.q: You follow the arrows → → ←, each arrow 1 square. Where are you at the end?
a: 1 square to the right of the start
1 square to the left of the start
3 squares to the right of the start
80772.e: Twice to the right and once to the left: 2 minus 1 makes 1. You are 1 square to the right of the start.
80772.m: An arrow in the opposite direction cancels out a step.

80773.q: Which arrow points in the opposite direction to ↑?
80773.e: The opposite of up is down. That is why ↓ is the opposite direction.
80773.m: Opposite directions are up and down, and left and right.

80774.q: You follow the arrows ↑ → ↓ ←, each arrow 1 square. Where are you at the end?
a: 1 square to the right of the start
80774.e: You go once round in a circle: up, right, down, left. That brings you back to the start.
80774.m: If you go each direction once, you come back to the start.

80775.q: You draw one arrow for each square. How many arrows do you need for 3 squares to the right?
80775.e: Each square needs its own arrow. For 3 squares that is 3 arrows →.
80775.m: One arrow stands for one step.

80776.q: A grid has 3 rows with 3 squares each. How many squares is that?
80776.m: You count the squares of a grid as rows times squares per row.

80777.q: A grid has 4 rows with 4 squares each. How many squares is that?
80777.e: 4 times 4 makes 16. The grid has 16 squares.

80778.q: A grid has the columns A, B, C from left to right and the rows 1, 2, 3. Which square is to the right of B2?
80778.e: To the right of column B is column C. The row stays 2, so it is square C2.
80778.m: A square in a grid has a letter and a number.

80779.q: The rows of a grid are numbered 1, 2, 3 from bottom to top. Which square is directly above B2?
80779.e: Above row 2 is row 3. The column stays B, so it is B3.
80779.m: When going up, only the row number changes.

80780.q: A robot moves from square A1 to square C1 in the same row. How many squares does it move?
80780.e: From A to B is 1 square, from B to C another 1 square. Together that is 2 squares.
80780.m: You do not count the start square when moving.

80781.q: A robot may only move straight, not diagonally. What is the smallest number of squares it moves from A1 to B2?
80781.e: It moves 1 square to the right and 1 square up. That is 2 squares.
80781.m: Without moving diagonally, a robot needs two steps for a corner.

80782.q: A robot may only move straight, not diagonally. What is the smallest number of squares it moves from A1 to C3?
80782.e: It moves 2 squares to the right and 2 squares up. 2 + 2 = 4 squares.
80782.m: You find the shortest route without diagonals by adding the horizontal and vertical steps.

80783.q: What do you call the horizontal lines of squares in a grid?
80783.e: Horizontal lines go from left to right. They are called rows.
80783.m: Rows run horizontally across the grid.

80784.q: What do you call the vertical lines of squares in a grid?
80784.e: Vertical lines go from top to bottom. They are called columns.
80784.m: Columns run vertically through the grid.

80785.q: Rule: If the traffic light is red, then you stand still. The traffic light is red. What do you do?
80785.e: The condition “the light is red” is true. That is why the then part applies: stand still.
80785.m: If the if part is true, you do the then part.

80786.q: Rule: If it gets dark, then the lamp comes on. It is getting dark. What happens?
80786.e: The condition “it gets dark” is met. That is why the lamp comes on.
80786.m: If the condition is met, the action happens.

80787.q: Rule: If the robot touches a wall, it turns round. Otherwise it carries on. It does not touch a wall. What does it do?
80787.e: The condition “touched a wall” is not true. That is why the otherwise part applies: carry on.
80787.m: If the if part is not true, the otherwise part applies.

80788.q: In computer science, what do you call the “If ...” part of an if-then rule?
80788.e: The if part is the condition. Only if it is true is the then part carried out.
80788.m: A condition decides whether something happens.

80789.q: Game: If I show red, you clap. If I show blue, you stamp. I show blue. What do you do?
80789.e: Blue goes with the rule “stamp”. That is why you stamp.
80789.m: Each condition has its own action.

80790.q: Rule: If a number is even, say “Yes”, otherwise say “No”. The number is 7. What do you say?
80790.e: 7 is an odd number. The condition is not true, so you say “No”.
80790.m: With an if-then rule, you check the condition first.

80791.q: An automatic door has the rule: If someone is standing in front of it, then it opens. What happens if you stand in front of it?
80791.e: A sensor notices that someone is standing in front of it. The condition is met, so the door opens.
80791.m: Automatic doors work with an if-then rule.

80792.q: Rule: If you have collected 3 stars, then you have won. You have 2 stars. Have you won?
80792.e: The condition requires 3 stars. You only have 2, so 3 minus 2 makes 1 star still missing.
80792.m: A condition must be completely met.

80793.q: Dance: clap twice, turn once. You repeat the whole thing twice. How many times do you clap?
80793.e: In each round you clap twice. With 2 rounds that is 2 + 2 = 4 times.
80793.m: With a repeated dance sequence, you count every round.

80794.q: Dance: Repeat 3 times: hop, turn. How many times do you turn?
80794.e: In each round you turn once. With 3 rounds that is 3 turns.
80794.m: Every command in the repetition happens in every round.

80795.q: Why are dance instructions similar to a program?
a: They have steps in a fixed order
80795.e: In dance instructions, the steps follow exactly one after another. A program works in just the same way.
80795.m: Dance instructions are like a program for people.

80796.q: Dance instructions show a foot symbol. Which movement goes with it?
80796.e: You stamp with your foot. That is why the foot symbol stands for stamping.
80796.m: Symbols in instructions show which part of the body moves.

80797.q: What do you need so that everyone in the group dances at the same time?
80797.e: If everyone listens to the same beat, they do the steps at the same time.
80797.m: A shared beat keeps a dance group together.

80798.q: Dance: right, left, right, left and so on. Which is the 5th step?
80798.e: Odd-numbered steps are right, even-numbered steps are left. The 5th step is therefore right.
80798.m: A pattern helps you predict the next step.

80799.q: Dance instructions have 4 steps. You dance them 3 times in a row. How many steps is that?

80800.q: In musical statues, the music suddenly stops. What must everyone do?
80800.e: In musical statues the rule is: music off means stand still. Anyone who moves is out.
80800.m: In musical statues you stand still when the music stops.

80801.q: What colour is a ripe acorn usually?
80801.e: Young acorns are green. When they are ripe in autumn, they turn brown and shiny.

80802.q: Why don’t we humans eat raw acorns?
80802.e: Acorns contain lots of tannins. These taste very bitter and are bad for your tummy when raw.
80802.m: Raw acorns are not for us humans.

80803.q: Which farm animals did people once drive into the woods in autumn to eat acorns?
80803.e: In the past farmers fed their pigs in oak woods in autumn. This was called pannage.
80803.m: Pigs used to eat acorns in the woods.

80804.q: On which playing cards is the acorn one of the four suits?
80804.e: German Swiss Jass cards have the suits acorns, bells, roses and shields. The French cards have hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades.
80804.m: In Jass there is a suit called acorns.

80805.q: What does the husk that beechnuts grow in look like?
80805.e: Beechnuts grow in a woody husk with soft spines. When it is ripe, it splits open into four flaps.
80805.m: The beechnut husk splits open in autumn.

80806.q: How many beechnuts are usually in one husk?
80806.e: Usually two beechnuts lie together in one husk.
80806.m: A beech husk usually holds two beechnuts.

80807.q: Why shouldn’t you eat lots of raw beechnuts?
80807.e: Raw beechnuts contain substances that can cause tummy ache and sickness in larger amounts. Roasted, they are easier to digest.
80807.m: Beechnuts are best eaten roasted, and only a few.

80808.q: What did people once press out of beechnuts?
80808.e: Beechnuts contain a lot of fat. Especially in hard times, people pressed oil for cooking from them.
80808.m: You can press oil from beechnuts.

80809.q: What do you call a year in which beeches bear especially many fruits?
80809.e: Beeches do not bear the same amount of fruit every year. In a mast year, especially many beechnuts hang on the trees.
