81844.m: The lesser celandine has yellow flowers.

81845.q: What is special about the flowers of the lesser celandine?
81845.e: The petals are very shiny, as if they had been varnished. You can see this especially in sunshine.

81846.q: What shape are the leaves of the lesser celandine?
81846.e: The leaves are roundish to heart-shaped. They are shiny green.
81846.m: The lesser celandine has heart-shaped leaves.

81847.q: Which vitamin is found in large amounts in young lesser celandine leaves?
81847.e: The young leaves contain lots of vitamin C. That is why they used to be important in spring.
81847.m: Young lesser celandine leaves have lots of vitamin C.

81848.q: The German name of the lesser celandine contains the old word “Scharbock”. What is a Scharbock?
81848.e: Scharbock is an old German word for scurvy. Sailors on long voyages often used to get this disease.
81848.m: Scharbock is an old name for a disease.

81849.q: What is true of lesser celandine leaves once the plant flowers?
81849.e: From flowering onwards, the leaves contain more poisonous substances. So you should not eat them any more then.
81849.m: Once it flowers, the lesser celandine is more poisonous.

81850.q: Where does the lesser celandine like to grow?
81850.e: The lesser celandine loves damp soil. You find it in broadleaved woods, hedges and parks.
81850.m: The lesser celandine likes it damp.

81851.q: What does the lesser celandine have on its roots?
81851.e: Little tubers sit on the roots. The plant stores food in them for the next year.
81851.m: The lesser celandine has little tubers.

81852.q: When do you plant tulip bulbs in the garden?
81852.e: You put tulip bulbs in the ground in autumn. They need the cold of winter to flower in spring.
81852.m: Tulip bulbs are planted in autumn.

81853.q: Which country is famous for its big tulip fields?
81853.e: In the Netherlands there are huge colourful tulip fields. Tulips are sold from there all over the world.
81853.m: The Netherlands is the land of tulips.

81854.q: Where do tulips originally come from?
81854.e: Wild tulips originally grow in Asia, for example in the mountains of Central Asia. They came to Europe by way of Turkey.

81855.q: How many petals does a simple tulip have?
81855.e: A simple tulip has six petals. They are arranged in two rings of three.

81856.q: What do tulips do when they are standing in a vase?
a: They lose all their colour at once
81856.e: Cut tulips keep growing in the vase. Their stems can get a few centimetres longer.
81856.m: Tulips keep growing in the vase.

81857.q: Which object does the name “tulip” come from?
81857.e: The name comes from an old word for turban. The flower looks a little like this headdress.
81857.m: The name tulip comes from turban.

81858.q: What must you not do with rare wild tulips in the mountains?
81858.e: Wild tulips are very rare in Switzerland, for example the Grengiols tulip in Valais. They are protected and must not be picked.
81858.m: You do not pick rare wild flowers.

81859.q: Nearly 400 years ago in Holland, how expensive was an especially rare tulip bulb?
a: As expensive as a loaf of bread
81859.e: Around 1637 tulip bulbs were in great demand in Holland. For rare varieties people paid as much as for a house.
81859.m: Rare tulip bulbs used to be very expensive.

81860.q: Which colour do tulips still not really come in today?
81860.e: Tulips come in lots of colours. But nobody has yet been able to breed a true, pure blue.
81860.m: There are no true blue tulips.

81861.q: What colour is the daffodil usually?
81861.e: The daffodil is usually bright yellow. It is a typical spring flower.

81862.q: In German the daffodil is called the “Easter bell”. Why?
a: It grows out of Easter eggs
It is only green at Easter
81862.e: The daffodil flowers in spring, often right around Easter. Its flower is shaped like a bell.

81863.q: Which group of plants does the daffodil belong to?
81863.e: The daffodil is a narcissus. The narcissi include many varieties with yellow or white flowers.

81864.q: What does the middle of a daffodil flower look like?
81864.e: In the middle the daffodil has a long tube. It looks like a little trumpet.
81864.m: The daffodil has a trumpet in the middle.

81865.q: Why is it better to put daffodils in a vase on their own?
a: Their sap makes other flowers wilt faster
They drink up all the water
81865.e: A slime runs into the water from freshly cut stems. It harms other flowers in the same vase.
81865.m: Put daffodils in a vase on their own.

81866.q: Which parts of the daffodil are poisonous?
81866.e: The whole daffodil is poisonous, especially the bulb. So you should not put it in your mouth.

81867.q: In which months does the daffodil flower?
81867.e: The daffodil is an early spring flower. It flowers in March and April.
81867.m: The daffodil flowers in March and April.

81868.q: Where in Switzerland are the meadows full of wild white narcissi famous in May?
81868.e: In May lots and lots of white narcissi flower in the meadows above Montreux. They are relatives of the daffodil.
81868.m: Many narcissi flower near Montreux in May.

81967.q: What does the biceps do to your arm?
81967.e: The biceps is at the front of the upper arm. When it contracts, the arm bends at the elbow.

81968.q: What does ‘bi’ mean in the word biceps?
81968.e: Biceps means ‘two-headed’. At the top, the muscle starts with two heads at the shoulder.

81969.q: What happens to the biceps when you bend your arm tightly?
81969.e: A muscle contracts when it works. That is why the biceps gets shorter and bulges like a little hill.
81969.m: A working muscle gets shorter and thicker.

81970.q: During which activity does your biceps work hard?
81970.e: When you lift a load, you bend your arm. The biceps has to pull hard to do this.
81970.m: The biceps works when you lift loads.

81971.q: How do children like to show off the ‘muscles’ on their upper arm?
a: Bend the arm and tense it
81971.e: When you bend your arm and tense it hard, you can see the biceps as a bulge. That is what ‘showing your muscles’ means.
81971.m: You can easily see a tensed biceps.

81972.q: Which joint does the biceps mainly move?
81972.e: The biceps pulls on the forearm. So it mainly moves the elbow joint.
81972.m: The biceps mainly moves the elbow.

81973.q: The biceps also helps to turn the hand. Which way does it turn the palm?
81973.e: The biceps turns the forearm so that the palm faces upwards. You need this, for example, when you hold soup on a spoon.
81973.m: The biceps turns the palm upwards.

81974.q: Can you move your biceps whenever you want?
81974.e: The biceps is a skeletal muscle. You can control muscles like this yourself, whenever you want.
81974.m: You control skeletal muscles by choice.

a: At the back of the lower leg
At the front of the thigh
At the back of the upper arm
At the bottom of the back
81975.e: The calf is the thick muscle at the back of the lower leg, between the knee and the heel.
81975.m: The calf is at the back of the lower leg.

81976.q: Which movement does the calf muscle make possible?
81976.e: The calf muscle pulls the heel upwards. That way you can stand on tiptoe.
81976.m: The calf muscle lifts you onto tiptoe.

81977.q: Why do racing cyclists often have very strong calves?
a: The calves work hard when pedalling
They eat a lot of bread
81977.e: When cycling, the legs push down on the pedals again and again. The calf muscles work too and become strong.

81978.q: What is it called when your calf suddenly goes very hard and hurts a lot?
81978.e: With a calf cramp, the muscle suddenly tightens and does not let go. This sometimes happens during sport or at night.
81978.m: A calf cramp is a suddenly hard, painful calf muscle.

81979.q: What usually helps with a calf cramp?
a: Gently pulling your toes towards you
Holding your breath for a long time
81979.e: If you gently pull your toes towards you, the calf is stretched. Then the cramp usually goes away soon.
81979.m: Gentle stretching helps with a calf cramp.

81980.q: What is the bone at the front of the lower leg, opposite the calf, called?
81980.e: At the front of the lower leg you can feel the shinbone directly under the skin. The soft calf is at the back.
81980.m: The shinbone is at the front of the lower leg.

81981.q: How does your calf feel when you stand on tiptoe on one leg?
81981.e: On tiptoe, the calf muscle carries your whole weight. So it is tightly tensed and feels hard.
81981.m: A working calf muscle feels hard.

81982.q: Where is the large gluteal muscle?
81982.e: The large gluteal muscle forms your bottom. It is at the back of the pelvis.
81982.m: The large gluteal muscle forms your bottom.

81983.q: Which muscle is one of the largest muscles in the body?
81983.e: The large gluteal muscle is very big and strong. Eyes, ears and fingers only have small muscles.
81983.m: The large gluteal muscle is one of the largest muscles.

81984.q: How does your gluteal muscle help you in everyday life?
81984.e: When you get up from a chair, the gluteal muscle straightens the hip. That helps you up.
81984.m: The gluteal muscle helps you stand up.

81985.q: What do humans especially need the strong gluteal muscle for?
81985.e: The gluteal muscle keeps the pelvis steady when we walk on two legs. That is why it is so strong in humans.
81985.m: The gluteal muscle helps us walk upright.

81986.q: Which way does the large gluteal muscle pull the leg?
81986.e: The large gluteal muscle pulls the thigh backwards. You need this for walking and running.
81986.m: The gluteal muscle pulls the leg backwards.

81987.q: Which part of your body do you sit on when you sit on a chair?
81987.e: When you sit, your weight rests on your bottom. The gluteal muscles help to cushion it.
81987.m: When you sit, your bottom carries your weight.

81988.q: There is the large, the medium and the ... gluteal muscle. Which word is missing?
81988.e: There are three gluteal muscles on your bottom: the large, the medium and the small one.

81989.q: During which movement does the gluteal muscle work especially hard?
81989.e: When climbing stairs, you have to push your body up step by step. The gluteal muscle works hard to do this.
81989.m: Climbing stairs trains the gluteal muscle.

81990.q: Which exercise trains the stomach muscles?
81990.e: With sit-ups you lift your upper body up from lying down. The stomach muscles do this work.

81991.q: What do you call clearly visible stomach muscles that look like little packets?
81991.e: A long stomach muscle is divided by strips of tendon running across it. In fit people this looks like six little packets.
81991.m: A six-pack is clearly visible stomach muscles.

81992.q: What do the stomach muscles protect?
81992.e: There are no bones at the front of the belly. The stomach muscles form a firm wall in front of the stomach and intestines.
81992.m: The stomach muscles protect the organs in the belly.

81993.q: What do the stomach muscles help with, together with the back muscles?
81993.e: The belly and back hold the upper body like two sides of a support. That way you can sit and stand upright.
81993.m: Your belly and back keep you upright.

81994.q: What do you feel in your belly when you cough hard?
81994.e: When you cough, the stomach muscles push the air out of the lungs forcefully. That is why you feel your belly getting hard.
81994.m: Your stomach muscles work when you cough.

81995.q: Why can your belly hurt after laughing for a long time?
a: The stomach muscles work a lot
81995.e: When you laugh, the stomach muscles tighten again and again. After laughing for a long time they are tired.

a: At the front and sides of the belly
81996.e: The stomach muscles are at the front and sides of the belly. They reach from the ribs to the pelvis.
81996.m: The stomach muscles are at the front of the belly.

81997.q: Which muscles help you turn your upper body to the side?
81997.e: At the sides of the belly there are stomach muscles that run diagonally. They turn and tilt the upper body.
81997.m: The stomach muscles turn the upper body.

81998.q: In which exercise do you hold your body straight as a board on your forearms?
81998.e: In the plank you rest on your forearms and toes. The stomach muscles keep your body straight.
81998.m: The plank strengthens the stomach muscles.

81999.q: When do you usually feel muscle soreness?
a: Straight away with the first step
81999.e: Muscle soreness usually only starts hours after sport. It is often strongest the next day or the day after.
81999.m: Muscle soreness usually comes the next day.

82000.q: Where does muscle soreness come from?
82000.e: Unusual effort causes very small tears in the muscle fibres. They heal again but hurt for a while.
82000.m: Muscle soreness comes from tiny tears in the muscle.

82001.e: The muscle needs time to heal. Gentle movement and a warm bath do many people good.
82001.m: Rest and gentle movement help with muscle soreness.

82002.q: How long does muscle soreness usually last?
82002.e: Muscle soreness has usually gone after a few days, at the latest after about a week.
82002.m: Muscle soreness goes away after a few days.

82003.q: After which activity are you more likely to get muscle soreness?
82003.e: You mainly get muscle soreness when a muscle has to do something new or very tiring.

82004.q: On which kind of hike do you easily get sore thigh muscles?
82004.e: When walking downhill, the thighs have to brake the body with every step. This braking work very easily causes muscle soreness.
82004.m: Walking downhill easily causes muscle soreness.

82005.e: Muscle soreness hurts but is harmless. The muscle repairs itself.
82005.m: Muscle soreness is harmless and heals by itself.

82006.q: You do the same new exercise every week. What happens to the muscle soreness over time?
a: It always stays just as strong
82006.e: The muscle gets used to the exercise. That is why you usually get less muscle soreness afterwards.
82006.m: With practice, muscle soreness gets weaker.

82007.q: Where do you get muscle soreness after lots of sit-ups?
82007.e: Muscle soreness happens in the muscles that have worked. After sit-ups, those are the stomach muscles.
82007.m: You feel muscle soreness in the muscles that have worked.

82008.q: Which muscles do you need to smile?
82008.e: There are many small muscles in the face. Some of them pull on the mouth when you smile.
82008.m: You need facial muscles to smile.

82009.q: Which way do muscles pull the corners of your mouth when you smile?
82009.e: When you smile, muscles in the cheeks pull the corners of your mouth up and to the side.
82009.m: When you smile, the corners of your mouth go up.

82010.q: What are many facial muscles directly attached to?
82010.e: Many facial muscles end directly in the skin. That is why the skin moves too when you smile.
82010.m: Many facial muscles pull directly on the skin.

82011.q: From what age do babies smile at people on purpose?
82011.e: At about six weeks, babies start to smile at people on purpose. This is called social smiling.
82011.m: Babies smile on purpose after about six weeks.

82012.q: What do you call all the movements of the face, such as smiling or frowning?
82012.e: With facial expressions we show feelings on our face. The facial muscles move the mouth, eyes and forehead to do this.
82012.m: Facial expressions show feelings on the face.

82013.q: How can you often recognise a real, happy smile?
a: By little creases around the eyes
82013.e: In a real smile, the muscles around the eyes work too. Then little laughter lines appear.
82013.m: In a real smile, the eyes smile too.

82014.q: Where in the world do people understand a smile as a friendly sign?
82014.e: A smile is a sign that people understand in almost every country. Even babies smile without learning to.
82014.m: A smile is understood almost everywhere.

82015.q: Which feeling does a smile usually show?
82015.e: People who are happy usually smile. The face shows how we are feeling.

82016.q: Which muscle helps you purse your lips to whistle?
a: The ring muscle of the mouth
82016.e: Around the lips there is a ring-shaped muscle. When it tightens, the lips purse, for example when you whistle.
82016.m: A ring muscle surrounds the mouth.

82017.q: What do you do with your legs when you take off for a high jump?
82017.e: Before the jump your knees are bent. When you take off, you straighten your legs powerfully and push yourself away from the ground.
82017.m: When you take off, you straighten your legs powerfully.

82018.q: Muscles can only pull. How does a bent arm become straight again?
a: A muscle on the other side pulls
82018.e: Because muscles can only pull, they work in pairs. One bends, the other on the opposite side straightens.
82018.m: Muscles work in pairs because they can only pull.

82019.q: Which muscle straightens the leg at the knee?
82019.e: At the front of the thigh there is a large muscle with four heads. It pulls the lower leg forwards and straightens the knee.
82019.m: The front thigh muscle straightens the knee.

82020.q: What do many people do in bed right after waking up?
82020.e: After sleeping, many people have a good long stretch. It wakes up the muscles.
82020.m: Stretching wakes up the muscles in the morning.

82021.q: In which yoga pose does your body form an upside-down V?
82021.e: In downward dog, your hands and feet are on the floor and your bottom points upwards. Your back, arms and legs stretch.
82021.m: Downward dog is a yoga pose.

82022.q: What does your arm do at the end of a long throw?
82022.e: When throwing, the arm swings forwards and is fully straightened at the end. That way the ball flies far.
82022.m: When throwing, the arm is straightened.

82023.q: Which part of the body do gymnasts stretch out nice and long in many exercises?
82023.e: In gymnastics, pointed toes show a clean posture. That is why gymnasts pay attention to them.
82023.m: In gymnastics you point your toes.

82024.q: What is the opposite of straightening?
82024.e: When straightening, a joint is made straight. When bending, it is angled.

82025.q: What is the exercise called where you bend your knees and stand up again?
82025.e: In a squat you go down with bent knees and straighten up again.
82025.m: In a squat you bend your knees.

82026.q: At which joint do you bend your leg when you kneel down?
82026.e: When you kneel down, you bend your leg sharply at the knee.
82026.m: When you kneel, you bend your knee.

82027.q: What do you bend when you grip a ball tightly?
82027.e: To grip, you curl your fingers around the ball. Your fingers are bent as you do so.
82027.m: When gripping, I bend my fingers.

82028.q: What do you do with your knees before you jump up high?
82028.e: Before the jump you bend your knees. Then you straighten your legs powerfully and jump up.
82028.m: Before jumping, I bend my knees.

82029.q: What do you do with your fingers when you make a fist?
82029.e: To make a fist, you curl all your fingers in. They are bent as you do so.
82029.m: In a fist, the fingers are bent.

82030.q: Why should you bend your knees when lifting a heavy box?
82030.e: With bent knees and a straight back, the strong leg muscles lift the load. This protects the back.
82030.m: Lift heavy things with bent knees.

82031.q: How do people in Japan often greet each other politely?
a: With a leap in the air
82031.e: In Japan, people often bend their upper body forwards as a greeting. This is called a bow.
82031.m: In Japan, people often greet with a bow.

82032.q: What do you bend when you bend forwards to your toes?
82032.e: When you bend down, your upper body folds forwards at the hip. The hip joint bends as you do so.
82032.m: When bending down, you bend your hip.

82033.q: What is the inside of the elbow called, which forms a crease when you bend it?
82033.e: On the inside of the elbow is the crook of the elbow. When you bend your arm, a crease forms there.
82033.m: The crook of the elbow is on the inside of the elbow.

82034.q: What can happen if a tendon is overloaded for a long time?
82034.e: Too much strain irritates the tendon. Then it can become inflamed and hurt until it has recovered.

82035.e: Tendons are made of strong fibres. They are very hard to tear, so they can withstand the pull of the muscle.

82036.q: Where can you see tendons clearly when you spread your fingers?
a: On the back of the hand
82036.e: Tendons run to the fingers on the back of the hand. When you spread your fingers, they stand out under the skin.
82036.m: You can see tendons on the back of the hand.

82037.q: What does a tendon do when its muscle tenses?
a: It comes away from the bone
82037.e: The muscle pulls on the tendon. The tendon passes the pull on to the bone, and the bone moves.
82037.m: The tendon passes the muscle’s pull on to the bone.

82038.q: Can a tendon contract by itself?
a: Yes, much more strongly than the muscle
82038.e: A tendon is like a strong rope. It cannot work by itself but only passes on the pull of the muscle.

82039.e: Tendons look whitish and shiny. Muscles, on the other hand, are red.

82040.q: What connects a muscle to the bone?
82040.e: A tendon is like a strong rope. It holds the muscle firmly to the bone.

82041.q: The doctor taps under the kneecap with a small hammer. What is she hitting there?
82041.e: Under the kneecap there is a strong tendon. If you tap on it, the lower leg kicks forwards.
82041.m: There is a tendon under the kneecap.

a: At the back, above the heel
At the front of the knee
82042.e: You can feel the Achilles tendon at the back of your foot, just above the heel.
82042.m: The Achilles tendon is at the back, above the heel.

82043.q: Which muscle does the Achilles tendon connect to the heel?
82043.e: The Achilles tendon connects the calf muscle to the heel bone. That way the calf can pull the heel up.
82043.m: The Achilles tendon connects the calf and the heel.

82044.q: Who is the Achilles tendon named after?
82044.e: Achilles is a hero from the ancient Greek legends. The tendon is named after him.
82044.m: The Achilles tendon is named after the hero Achilles.

82045.q: According to the legend, where could the hero Achilles be wounded?
82045.e: His mother dipped him into a magic river as a baby, holding him by the heel. So that was the only place he could be wounded.
82045.m: Achilles could only be wounded on his heel.

82046.q: What is special about the Achilles tendon?
82046.e: The Achilles tendon is the strongest tendon in the human body. It has to withstand a lot when walking, running and jumping.
82046.m: The Achilles tendon is the strongest tendon in the body.

82047.q: What do you call a weak spot, after the legend of Achilles?
82047.e: Because Achilles could only be wounded on his heel, a weak spot is called an Achilles heel today.
82047.m: A weak spot is called an Achilles heel.

82048.q: During which movement does the Achilles tendon have to withstand especially a lot?
82048.e: When jumping, the calf pulls very hard on the heel. The Achilles tendon then has to carry great forces.
82048.m: The Achilles tendon works hard when jumping.

82049.q: What is the right way to hold a stretch?
82049.e: When stretching, you move slowly into position and hold it calmly. Bouncing and jerking can injure the muscle.

82050.e: If you stretch often, you can move your joints further. So you become more flexible.

82051.e: When stretching, you should feel a slight pull. Strong pain is a sign that you are going too far.

82052.q: Roughly how long do you hold a stretch?
82052.e: You usually hold a stretch for about 15 to 30 seconds. Then you relax again.
82052.m: You hold a stretch for about half a minute.

82053.q: You put one leg far back and press the heel into the floor. What are you stretching?
82053.e: If the back heel stays on the floor and the leg is straight, the calf is stretched long.
82053.m: With your heel on the floor, you stretch your calf.

82054.q: You sit with straight legs and reach for your toes. What are you mainly stretching?
82054.e: When you reach for your toes, the muscles at the back of the thigh and calf are stretched.
82054.m: Reaching for your toes stretches the backs of your legs.

82055.q: In which sport do you need to be especially flexible?
82055.e: In rhythmic gymnastics you show the splits and wide movements. That is why the athletes stretch a lot.
82055.m: Gymnastics needs a lot of flexibility.

82056.q: When is the best time to stretch during training?
a: When the muscles are ice cold
Only in the middle of the night
82056.e: Warm muscles stretch better. That is why you stretch after warming up.

82057.q: You stand on one leg and pull your other foot towards your bottom. What are you stretching?
82057.e: When the foot is pulled towards the bottom, the front thigh muscle is stretched long.
82057.m: Foot to bottom stretches the front of the thigh.

82058.q: Which muscles work especially hard when skipping?
82058.e: When skipping, you hop off your toes again and again. This is done mainly by the calves.

82059.q: On which part of the foot do you land when skipping?
a: On the balls of the feet
On the top of the foot
82059.e: You land softly on the balls of your feet. That way your legs cushion the jump well.
82059.m: When skipping, you land on the balls of your feet.

82060.q: What happens to your heart when you skip?
82060.e: Skipping is tiring. The muscles need more blood, so the heart beats faster.
82060.m: When skipping, your heart beats faster.

82061.q: You stand in the middle of the rope. Roughly how far up should the handles reach?
82061.e: A skipping rope of the right size reaches about up to your armpits with its handles. If it is too short or too long, you trip easily.
82061.m: A skipping rope reaches about up to your armpits.

82062.q: What is a jump called where the rope swings under your feet twice?
82062.e: In a double under, the rope turns twice during one jump. To do it you have to jump high and turn fast.
82062.m: In a double under, the rope turns twice.

82063.q: In the game with the long rope, how many children usually swing the rope?
82063.e: With the long rope, two children hold the ends and swing it. The others jump in the middle.
82063.m: With the long rope, usually two children swing it.

82064.q: What do you mainly swing the rope with when skipping?
82064.e: Your elbows stay close to your body. You turn the rope mainly with small movements of your wrists.
82064.m: You turn a skipping rope with your wrists.

82065.q: What is best to wear on your feet when skipping?
82065.e: Trainers cushion the many jumps and give good grip.

82066.q: What do you need scales for?
a: To measure how heavy something is
To measure what time it is
To measure how long something is
To measure how warm it is
82066.e: Scales show how heavy an object is. There are other measuring instruments for time, length and warmth.
82066.m: With scales you measure how heavy something is.

82067.q: Where do you often need scales when shopping?
82067.e: Fruit and vegetables are often bought loose. The price depends on how much they weigh.
82067.m: Fruit and vegetables are often weighed.

82068.q: What are scales a well-known symbol of?
82068.e: The figure of Lady Justice holds scales in her hand. The scales show that both sides are weighed up fairly.
82068.m: Scales are a symbol of justice.

82069.q: Why is a parcel weighed at the post office?
a: The price depends on the weight
So that it does not get wet
So that it looks more colourful
82069.e: At the post office, a heavy parcel costs more than a light one. That is why you need to know how much it weighs.

82070.q: How do digital scales show the weight?
82070.e: Digital scales measure electronically and show the result as a number on a small display.
82070.m: Digital scales show the weight as a number.

82071.q: How can you weigh a whole lorry?
a: With lots of bathroom scales in the house
82071.e: For lorries there are large scales built into the ground. The lorry simply drives onto them.

82072.q: Why is a baby often weighed?
a: To see whether it is growing well
82072.e: If a baby gains weight regularly, it is growing well. That is why it is weighed at the doctor's or at the baby clinic.
82072.m: Babies are weighed to check their growth.

82073.q: What should scales show when there is nothing on them yet?
82073.e: Without a load, the scales should start at zero. Only then will they measure the correct weight afterwards.

82074.q: Who needs very precise scales for tiny amounts?
82074.e: Gold is very expensive. That is why a goldsmith weighs even the tiniest amounts very precisely.
82074.m: For gold you need very precise scales.

82075.q: How many pans does a simple beam balance have?
82075.e: A beam balance has a beam with one pan on the left and one on the right.
82075.m: A beam balance has two pans.

82076.q: On a beam balance there is more on the left than on the right. What happens?
82076.e: The heavier side is pulled down more strongly. So it sinks, and the lighter side goes up.
82076.m: On a beam balance the heavier side sinks.

82077.q: When is the beam of a beam balance completely level?
a: When both sides are equally heavy
When there is more on the left
When there is more on the right
When only one pan holds something
82077.e: If both sides are equally heavy, neither side pulls more strongly. Then the beam is level.
82077.m: Equally heavy sides keep the beam level.

82078.q: Around which point does the beam of a beam balance tip?
a: Around the pivot in the middle
82078.e: The beam rests on a pivot in the middle. It tips left or right around this point.
82078.m: The beam turns around a point in the middle.

82079.q: Which piece of playground equipment works in a similar way to a beam balance?
82079.e: A seesaw is also a beam with a pivot in the middle. The heavier side goes down.
82079.m: A seesaw works like a beam balance.

82080.q: Roughly how old is the invention of the beam balance?
82080.e: People already weighed things with beam balances in ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia. It is one of the oldest measuring instruments.
82080.m: The beam balance is several thousand years old.

82081.q: Which object from the wardrobe can you use to make a simple beam balance?
82081.e: You hang up the coat hanger and attach a cup on the left and on the right. And you have a beam balance.
82081.m: A coat hanger can be a beam balance.

82082.q: What does a beam balance actually do?
82082.e: A beam balance does not show a number. It only shows which side is heavier or whether both are equally heavy.

82083.q: Where are bathroom scales often kept at home?
82083.e: Many families keep their scales in the bathroom. There they stand on a hard floor.
82083.m: Bathroom scales are often kept in the bathroom.

82084.q: In which unit do bathroom scales in Switzerland show weight?
82084.e: In Switzerland, body weight is measured in kilograms, kg for short.
82084.m: Body weight is measured in kilograms.

82085.q: Why shouldn't bathroom scales stand on a thick carpet?
82085.e: On a soft carpet, the scales stand crooked and sink in. Then they often show the wrong weight.
82085.m: Bathroom scales need a hard floor.

82086.q: How do you stand on bathroom scales correctly?
82086.e: Only if you stand still can the scales measure correctly. If you jump, the display jumps back and forth.
82086.m: You stand still on the scales.

82087.q: Who often measures children's weight and height at a check-up?
82087.e: At the children's doctor, they check whether a child is growing well. For this they measure weight and height.
82087.m: The children's doctor measures weight and height.

82088.q: You weigh 25 kg and your friend weighs 27 kg. You stand on the scales together. What do they show?
82088.e: The scales measure both of you together. You calculate 25 kg + 27 kg = 52 kg.
82088.m: Together you weigh the sum of both weights.

82089.q: How can you weigh your cat on the bathroom scales?
a: Weigh yourself with and without the cat and subtract
Put the cat on the scales alone
Put the scales on the cat
82089.e: Cats rarely stand still. You weigh yourself with the cat in your arms, then without it. The difference is the cat's weight.
82089.m: You can weigh yourself with and without an animal and work out the difference.

82090.q: With your dog in your arms the scales show 40 kg, without the dog 32 kg. How heavy is the dog?
82090.e: The difference is the dog's weight. You calculate 40 kg minus 32 kg = 8 kg.
82090.m: You find the difference by subtracting.

82091.q: What do you need kitchen scales for?
82091.e: When cooking and baking you often have to weigh flour, sugar and butter exactly. That is what kitchen scales are for.
82091.m: You weigh ingredients with kitchen scales.

82092.q: In which unit do kitchen scales usually show the flour?
82092.e: For ingredients you need small amounts. That is why kitchen scales usually show grams.
82092.m: Kitchen scales usually measure in grams.

82093.q: What is the button on kitchen scales called that takes away the weight of the bowl?
82093.e: With the tare button you set the scales to zero with the empty bowl on them. Then they only measure the ingredients.
82093.m: With the tare button you take away the weight of the bowl.

82094.q: For a cake you need 200 g of sugar. There are already 150 g on the scales. How much is missing?
82094.e: You calculate 200 g minus 150 g = 50 g. So 50 g of sugar is still missing.
82094.m: You find what is missing by subtracting.

82095.q: What can you not weigh well on kitchen scales?
82095.e: Kitchen scales are made for small amounts, usually only up to a few kilograms. A bike is too big and too heavy.
82095.m: Kitchen scales are made for small amounts.

82096.q: Why do you weigh ingredients exactly when baking?
a: So that the cake turns out well
So that the oven heats up faster
So that the flour stays white
So that the bowl does not break
82096.e: When baking, the amounts must fit well together. If they are wrong, the cake may be too dry, for example.

82097.q: What do digital kitchen scales usually need in order to work?
82097.e: Digital scales measure with electronics. They usually get their electricity from a battery.

82098.q: You have weighed out 300 g of flour but only need half. How much is that?
82098.e: Half of 300 g is 300 g ÷ 2 = 150 g.
82098.m: You get half by dividing by two.

82099.q: Which of these weighs more than a kilogram?
82099.e: A big watermelon weighs several kilograms. A strawberry, a pencil and a teaspoon weigh only a few grams.
82099.m: A big watermelon weighs several kilograms.

82100.e: A litre of water weighs about one kilogram. That is a good help for estimating.
82100.m: A litre of water weighs about one kilogram.

82101.q: How heavy is a packet of sugar in the shop often?
82101.e: Sugar is often sold in packets of 1 kilogram. It says so on the packet.
82101.m: A packet of sugar often weighs 1 kilogram.

82102.q: Where was the original kilogram kept, which all other kilograms were based on?
82102.e: The original kilogram was a small metal cylinder. For a long time it was kept in a safe in Sèvres near Paris.
82102.m: The original kilogram was kept near Paris.

82103.q: A sack of potatoes weighs 2 kg and a sack of carrots 3 kg. How much do they weigh together?

82104.q: How much is half a kilogram?
82104.e: One kilogram is 1000 grams. Half of that is 500 grams.

82105.q: What do you measure in kilograms?
82105.e: The kilogram is a unit of weight. There are other units for length, warmth and time.
82105.m: The kilogram is a unit of weight.

82106.q: Roughly how much does a six-year-old child weigh?
82106.e: Many children weigh about 20 kilograms at six years old. But every child is different.
82106.m: A six-year-old child weighs about 20 kilograms.

82107.e: A small paper clip weighs about one gram. So a gram is very light.

82108.q: How much does an ordinary bar of chocolate weigh?
82108.e: Most bars of chocolate weigh 100 grams. It says so on the wrapper.
82108.m: An ordinary bar of chocolate weighs 100 grams.

82109.q: You have two packs of butter of 250 grams each. How much is that together?

82110.q: Which is more: 900 grams or 1 kilogram?
82110.e: 1 kilogram is 1000 grams. That is 100 grams more than 900 grams.

82111.q: Roughly how much does a five-franc coin weigh?
82111.e: A five-franc coin weighs about 13 grams. It is the heaviest Swiss coin in circulation today.
82111.m: A five-franc coin weighs about 13 grams.

82112.q: Which animal is so light that it is weighed in grams?
82112.e: A house mouse weighs only about 20 to 25 grams. Cows, horses and bears weigh many kilograms.
82112.m: A mouse weighs only a few grams.

82113.q: What weighs much less than a gram?
82113.e: An ant is so light that, depending on the kind, hundreds of ants together weigh only about one gram.
82113.m: An ant weighs much less than a gram.

82114.e: A brick is made of firm, dense fired clay. It is much heavier than a feather, a leaf or a soap bubble.

82115.q: A wooden ball and an iron ball are the same size. Which is heavier?
82115.e: Iron is much denser than wood. So if they are the same size, the iron ball is heavier.
82115.m: The same size does not mean the same weight.

82116.q: One balloon is filled with water, another of the same size with air. Which is heavier?
82116.e: Water is much heavier than air. That is why the water balloon is heavier.

82117.e: A sheet of paper weighs only a few grams. The other things are much heavier.
82117.m: A sheet of paper is very light.

82118.q: Without scales, how can you find out which of two things is heavier?
82118.e: With your hands you can feel which thing pulls down more strongly. That way you can compare roughly.
82118.m: You can compare weights with your hands.

82119.q: Which animal is the heaviest animal in the world?
82119.e: The blue whale is the heaviest animal that has ever lived. It can weigh well over 100 tonnes.
82119.m: The blue whale is the heaviest animal.

82120.q: Why is a wet bath towel heavier than a dry one?
a: Because there is water in it
82120.e: The towel soaks up water. The water has a weight, so the wet towel is heavier.

82121.q: On a beam balance there are 3 identical cubes on the left and 2 on the right. How many cubes must you add on the right?
82121.e: For both sides to be equally heavy, the right side also needs 3 cubes. You calculate 3 minus 2 = 1.
82121.m: For balance, both sides must be equally heavy.

82122.q: Why does a tightrope walker often carry a long pole?
82122.e: The long pole makes it easier to correct a tilt. So the tightrope walker keeps her balance better.
82122.m: A long pole helps with balance.

82123.q: Where must you place a ruler on your finger so that it does not fall off?
82123.e: For an even ruler, the middle is the balance point. There the weight on the left and right is the same.
82123.m: A ruler balances in the middle.

82124.q: Which tower of building blocks stands most safely?
a: Wide at the bottom and narrow at the top
Narrow at the bottom and wide at the top
82124.e: A wide base and a light top part make a tower stable. Then it does not tip over so easily.
82124.m: A tower stands safely when it is wide at the bottom.

82125.q: An apple weighs the same as 2 mandarins. How many mandarins weigh the same as 3 apples?
82125.e: Each apple equals 2 mandarins. You calculate 3 × 2 = 6.

82126.q: Why does a roly-poly toy always stand back up again?
a: Because it is heavy at the bottom
Because there is a battery inside
Because it is filled with air
82126.e: There is a heavy weight in its round base. It always pulls the roly-poly toy back upright.
82126.m: A heavy base keeps things upright.

82127.q: There is 1 kg on the left of the balance and 500 g on the right. How much is missing on the right for it to balance?
82127.e: 1 kg is 1000 g. You calculate 1000 g minus 500 g = 500 g.

82128.q: Which animal uses its long, bushy tail to keep its balance when climbing?
82128.e: The squirrel steers and balances with its tail. That way it jumps safely from branch to branch.
82128.m: The squirrel balances with its tail.

a: A hanging, moving work of art
82129.e: A mobile is made of rods, threads and figures. It hangs from the ceiling and moves gently.
82129.m: A mobile is a moving hanging work of art.

82130.q: Which artist made the mobile famous?
82130.e: The American Alexander Calder built moving hanging sculptures from about 1930. This made the mobile known all over the world.
82130.m: Alexander Calder made the mobile famous.

82131.q: What sets a mobile without a motor in motion?
82131.e: Even a light draught moves the figures. That is why a mobile often turns all by itself.

82132.q: Where is a mobile often hung?
82132.e: Babies like watching the turning figures. That is why a mobile is often hung over the baby's cot.
82132.m: A mobile often hangs over a baby's cot.

82133.q: A rod of a mobile hangs crooked because the figure on the left is heavier. Where do you move the hanging thread?
82133.e: The heavy figure needs a shorter distance to the hanging point. If you move the thread towards it, the rod hangs straight again.
82133.m: The hanging point belongs closer to the heavy side.

82134.e: Mobile means able to move. A mobile is called that because its parts move.

82135.q: Two fish of the same weight hang the same distance from the middle of a mobile rod. How does the rod hang?
82135.e: Equal weights at equal distances pull equally hard. So the rod is balanced and hangs level.
82135.m: Equal weights at equal distances keep the rod level.

82136.q: What can you make a simple mobile from?
82136.e: Light rods such as twigs, plus threads and paper figures: that is all you need for a simple mobile.
82136.m: You make a mobile from light parts.

82137.q: What is inside a spring balance?
82137.e: Inside a spring balance there is a coiled metal spring.
82137.m: There is a metal spring inside a spring balance.

82138.q: What does a spring balance usually have at the bottom for hanging things on?
82138.e: At the bottom end of the spring there is a hook. You hang the object you want to weigh on it.
82138.m: A spring balance has a hook at the bottom.

82139.q: A weight stretches the spring by 2 cm. How far does a weight twice as heavy stretch it?
82139.e: On a spring balance, twice the weight stretches the spring twice as far. You calculate 2 cm × 2 = 4 cm.
82139.m: Twice the weight stretches the spring twice as far.

82140.q: How do you use a spring balance?
a: You hang the object on it
82140.e: You hold the spring balance at the top. You hang the object on it at the bottom.
82140.m: You hang the object on a spring balance.

82141.q: What happens if you pull a spring apart far too much?
82141.e: If a spring is overstretched, it no longer goes all the way back. Then the spring balance measures wrongly.
82141.m: An overstretched spring stays worn out.

82142.q: What else is a spring balance called in physics lessons?
82142.e: With a spring balance you measure how strongly something pulls. That is why it is also called a force meter.
82142.m: A spring balance is a force meter.

82143.q: What does the spring do when you take the weight off again?
82143.e: A good spring is elastic. Without a weight, it springs back to its old length.
82143.m: Without a weight, a spring goes back again.

82144.q: Where do you read the weight on a spring balance?
a: From the colour of the spring
From the size of the hook
From the thickness of the spring
82144.e: Next to the spring there is a scale with lines and numbers. A pointer shows how far the spring is pulled.
82144.m: You read a spring balance on a scale.

82145.q: What do anglers often use to weigh their catch right by the water?
82145.e: A spring balance is small and light. You simply hang the fish on the hook.
82145.m: A spring balance is easy to take with you.

82146.q: How many kilograms are in a tonne?
82146.e: A tonne is 1000 kilograms. You use it for very heavy things.

82147.q: How do you abbreviate the unit tonne?
82147.e: The tonne is abbreviated with a small t, for example 2 t.

82148.e: A small car weighs about one tonne. A bike, a dog and a school bag are much lighter.
82148.m: A small car weighs about one tonne.

82149.q: Roughly how much can a fully grown bull elephant weigh?
82149.e: Large African bull elephants can weigh about 6 tonnes. That is 6000 kilograms.
82149.m: A bull elephant weighs several tonnes.

82150.e: A tonne is 1000 kg. You calculate 3 × 1000 kg = 3000 kg.
82150.m: To change tonnes into kilograms, multiply by 1000.

82151.q: A sign in front of a bridge says “3.5 t”. What does it mean?
a: Heavier vehicles may not cross it
82151.e: The sign gives the maximum weight. Vehicles heavier than 3.5 tonnes may not cross the bridge.
82151.m: A weight sign protects bridges from vehicles that are too heavy.

82152.q: Which of these is more likely to be given in tonnes?
82152.e: Tonnes are used for very heavy things, for example ships' cargoes.
82152.m: Very heavy things are measured in tonnes.

82153.e: 1000 kg is one tonne. You calculate 2000 kg ÷ 1000 = 2, so 2 tonnes.
82153.m: To change kilograms into tonnes, divide by 1000.

82154.q: How many kilograms are half a tonne?
82154.e: A tonne is 1000 kg. Half of that is 500 kg.

82155.q: What is a weight (as used with a balance)?
a: A piece with an exactly known weight
82155.e: A weight weighs exactly as much as is written on it. You can use it to weigh other things.
82155.m: A weight has an exactly known weight.

82156.q: What do you need weights for with a beam balance?
a: You put them on the other side
You stick them to the floor
You hang them from the ceiling
You throw them into the air
82156.e: The object goes on one pan and the weights on the other. When the beam is level, you know the weight.
82156.m: Weights go on the other side of the beam balance.

82157.q: What are weights for balances usually made of today?
82157.e: Weights are usually made of metal such as brass or steel. Metal hardly wears away and keeps its weight.
82157.m: Weights are usually made of metal.

82158.q: On a beam balance, weights of 100 g, 50 g and 20 g balance an apple. How heavy is the apple?
82158.e: You add up all the weights: 100 g + 50 g + 20 g = 170 g.

82159.q: There are 200 g of flour on the left. On the right there are weights of 100 g and 50 g. Which weight is still missing?
82159.e: There are already 100 g + 50 g = 150 g on the right. To make 200 g, 200 g minus 150 g = 50 g is still missing.
82159.m: You find the missing weight by subtracting.

82160.q: Why are small, precise weights in the laboratory handled with tweezers?
a: So that no grease or dirt gets on them
82160.e: Even grease from your fingers changes the weight a tiny bit. With tweezers the weights stay clean and precise.
82160.m: Precise weights are not touched with your fingers.

82161.q: What is written on a weight for a balance?
82161.e: Every weight has its weight printed or stamped on it, for example 100 g.
82161.m: A weight has its weight written on it.

82162.q: Which two weights make exactly 300 g together?
82162.e: You calculate 200 g + 100 g = 300 g. The other pairs make 250 g, 200 g or 350 g.

82262.e: When layers of rock are pushed together from the side, they bend. This makes a fold in the rock.
82262.m: A rock fold is made of bent layers of rock.

82263.q: What happens to layers of rock when they are pushed together from two sides?
82263.e: The layers cannot get out of the way and bend up and down. We say they are folded.
82263.m: Rock layers that are pushed together fold.

82265.q: Which Swiss mountain range in the north-west is made of many beautiful folds?
82265.e: The Jura is made of long, folded chains of limestone. That is why it is called the Folded Jura.
82265.m: The Jura is a fold mountain range.

82266.q: Which two big tectonic plates collided and folded up the Alps?
82266.e: The African Plate pushed against the European Plate. Layers of rock were folded and piled up into the Alps.
82266.m: Africa pushed against Europe, and that is how the Alps formed.

82267.q: Where in the mountains can you often see rock folds well?
82267.e: On steep rock faces the rock is exposed. You can see the bent layers well there.
82267.m: You can often see rock folds on rock faces.

82268.q: How long does it take for rock to bend into a big fold?
82268.e: Rock only moves very slowly. Big folds take millions of years to form.
82268.m: Rock folds form over millions of years.

82269.q: How do layers of rock lie at first, before they are folded?
a: Flat on top of each other
82269.e: Layers often form on the seabed and at first lie flat on top of each other. Only later can they be bent.
82269.m: Rock layers first lie flat on top of each other.

82270.q: Which is the highest mountain in Switzerland?
82270.e: No other summit in Switzerland is higher. It lies near the border with Italy.
82270.m: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

82271.q: Roughly how high is the Dufourspitze?
82271.e: The Dufourspitze is 4634 metres high. That makes it the highest summit in Switzerland.
82271.m: The Dufourspitze is over 4000 metres high.

82272.q: Which big mountain massif does the Dufourspitze belong to?
82272.e: The Dufourspitze is the highest summit in the Monte Rosa massif. This massif has several summits over 4000 metres.
82272.m: The Dufourspitze belongs to Monte Rosa.

82273.q: Which summit is the highest point in Switzerland?
82273.e: The Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is about 4634 metres high. It is named after General Henri Dufour.
82273.m: The Dufourspitze is the highest mountain in Switzerland.

82275.q: What covers the Dufourspitze all year round?
82275.e: At over 4600 metres it is always cold. That is why there is snow and ice there all year round.
82275.m: The Dufourspitze is covered in snow all year round.

82276.e: Lots of loose stones collect below rock faces. They form a steep slope, the scree slope.
82276.m: A scree slope is a slope of loose stones.

82277.q: Where do you usually find scree slopes?
82277.e: Stones break off the rock faces and fall down. They collect into a slope at the foot of the face.
82277.m: Scree slopes lie below rock faces.

82278.q: What breaks stones off the rocks, which then fall onto the scree slope?
82278.e: Water gets into cracks and freezes into ice. Ice needs more space and so breaks pieces off the rock, especially when it often freezes and thaws again.
82278.m: Freezing water breaks stones off the rock.

82279.q: Why is it dangerous to walk across a scree slope?
82279.e: The stones lie loosely on top of each other. If you step on them, they can slide away.
82279.m: On scree slopes, the stones slip easily.

82280.q: Which alpine animal likes living among the stones of scree slopes and whistles when there is danger?
82280.e: Marmots live in burrows among stones and meadows. When there is danger, they warn the others with a loud whistle.
82280.m: Marmots whistle when there is danger.

82281.q: What shape does a scree slope often have?
a: Like a cone or a fan
82281.e: The stones fall down at one spot and spread out downwards. This often makes a cone or a fan.
82281.m: A scree slope is often shaped like a cone.

82282.q: Where on a scree slope are the biggest stones usually found?
82282.e: Big, heavy stones roll further when they fall. That is why they usually lie at the foot of the slope.
82282.m: The biggest stones roll furthest down the slope.

82283.q: What is another word for a scree slope?
82283.e: A scree slope is also called a talus slope. Both mean a slope of loose rock debris.
82283.m: A scree slope is also called a talus slope.

a: An opening at the end of the glacier
A door to a ski hut
82284.e: At the lower end of a glacier there is often a big opening in the ice. Meltwater flows out there.
82284.m: A glacier portal is an opening at the end of the glacier.

82285.q: What comes out of a glacier portal?
82285.e: Meltwater collects under the glacier. It comes out at the glacier portal as a glacier stream.
82285.m: A glacier stream flows out of the glacier portal.

82286.q: What colour is the water from a glacier portal often?
82286.e: The water carries finely ground rock with it. That is why it looks cloudy and milky grey.

82287.q: What is the cloudy water called that flows out of the glacier portal?
82287.e: The water is full of the finest rock flour. Because it is so cloudy, it is called glacier milk.
82287.m: Cloudy glacier water is called glacier milk.

82288.q: Why should you not go into a glacier portal?
82288.e: The ice at the glacier portal is melting and is often brittle. Big pieces of ice can suddenly fall down.
82288.m: Ice can break off at the glacier portal.

82289.q: When does the most water flow out of a glacier portal?
82289.e: When it is warm, a lot of ice melts. That is why there is the most water in the glacier stream on summer afternoons.
82289.m: The most glacier water flows on summer afternoons.

82290.q: Which big river begins at a glacier in Valais?
82290.e: The Rhône rises at the Rhône Glacier in Valais. Its water comes from the glacier's meltwater.
82290.m: The Rhône begins at the Rhône Glacier.

82291.q: Why does a glacier portal change from year to year?
a: It is walled up with stones
82291.e: A glacier flows slowly and melts away at its end. That is why its portal keeps changing.

82292.e: A pass is a lower point between mountains. A path or road leads there from one valley to another.
82292.m: A mountain pass leads over the mountains.

82293.q: Which pass links the canton of Uri with Ticino?
82293.e: The Gotthard Pass leads from Andermatt in the canton of Uri to Airolo in Ticino. It is one of the best-known passes in the Alps.
82293.m: The Gotthard Pass links Uri with Ticino.

82294.q: Why are many passes closed in winter?
a: Because of floods in the sea
82294.e: In winter there is a lot of snow on the passes. Avalanches make the roads dangerous, so they are closed.
82294.m: Many passes are closed in winter because of snow.

82295.q: Which dogs is the Great St Bernard Pass famous for?
82295.e: The monks on the Great St Bernard bred St Bernard dogs. In the past the dogs helped to find travellers in the snow.
82295.m: St Bernard dogs come from the Great St Bernard.

82296.q: What is a house on a pass called where travellers used to find shelter?
82296.e: A hospice is a lodging on a pass. Travellers found food and a warm bed there.
82296.m: A hospice gave travellers shelter on the pass.

82297.q: What are the tight bends called that a road often uses to climb up to a pass?
82297.e: On steep slopes the road zigzags back and forth in many tight bends. These bends are called hairpin bends or switchbacks.
82297.m: Pass roads often have lots of hairpin bends.

82298.q: What was built so that people can cross the Gotthard safely in winter too?
82298.e: Today railway and road tunnels go through the Gotthard. That way you can get from north to south even when it snows.

82299.q: Which two things does a mountain pass connect?
82299.e: A pass leads up out of one valley and down into another valley on the other side. That is how it connects two valleys.

a: A very steep slope of rock
A flat stone by a stream
82300.e: A rock face is a steep, often almost vertical surface of rock. You find them on many mountains.
82300.m: A rock face is a steep slope of rock.

82301.q: Which famous rock face is in the Bernese Oberland?
82301.e: The Eiger North Face is about 1800 metres high. It is one of the best-known climbing walls in the Alps.
82301.m: The Eiger North Face is a famous rock face.

82302.q: Who climbs rock faces with a rope and a helmet?
82302.e: Climbers go up rock faces with a rope, harness and helmet. The rope protects them if they fall.
82302.m: Climbers secure themselves on the rock face with a rope.

82303.q: Which big bird of prey often builds its nest on rock faces?
82303.e: The golden eagle likes to build its eyrie on steep rock faces. There it is safe from enemies.
82303.m: The golden eagle likes to nest on rock faces.

82304.q: In which valley do the Staubbach Falls plunge over a high rock face?
82304.e: The Lauterbrunnen valley has very steep rock faces. Lots of waterfalls plunge down them, for example the Staubbach Falls.
82304.m: The Lauterbrunnen valley has high rock faces and waterfalls.

82305.q: Why do you need to be careful at the foot of a rock face?
a: The ground is made of glass
82305.e: Stones keep coming loose from a rock face. That is why it is dangerous at the foot of the face.
82305.m: Stones can fall down below rock faces.

82306.q: What is an easy climbing route with fixed steel cables and ladders called?
82306.e: On a via ferrata, steel cables, rungs and ladders are fixed to the rock. You clip yourself in with a special set and are protected that way.
82306.m: A via ferrata has fixed steel cables on the rock.

82307.q: Which animal with big curved horns climbs skilfully on rock faces?
82307.e: The ibex has hooves that grip well on rock. It climbs safely over steep rocks.
82307.m: The ibex climbs skilfully on rock.

82308.e: In a rockfall, stones come loose from a slope or a rock face. They fall or bounce down.

82309.q: What protects your head from falling stones when climbing?
82309.e: A hard helmet stops falling stones. That is why climbers and mountaineers wear a helmet.
82309.m: A helmet protects your head from falling stones.

82310.q: What is put up along mountain roads to protect cars from falling stones?
82310.e: Strong steel nets catch falling stones. That keeps roads and railway lines safer.

a: When ice in the rock thaws
When there is no wind in winter
When it has been dry for a long time
At night during a full moon
82311.e: Ice holds loose stones in place like glue. When it thaws, the stones come loose and fall down.
82311.m: There is often rockfall when things thaw.

82312.q: What should you shout if you kick a stone loose yourself?
82312.e: By shouting “Rock!” loudly, you warn people further down. Then they can protect themselves.
82312.m: If you kick a stone loose, shout “Rock!” loudly.

82313.q: What does a road sign with falling stones on it show?
82313.e: The sign warns of stones that can fall onto the road. You should not stop there.
82313.m: The sign with falling stones warns of rockfall.

82314.q: How should you behave on a path where there is a danger of falling rocks?
a: Stop for a long time and have a picnic
82314.e: Where stones can fall, you do not stand still. You keep walking briskly until you are out of the danger zone.
82314.m: Do not take a break in rockfall zones.

82315.q: What is a roof over a road called that protects it from stones and avalanches?
82315.e: A gallery is a strong concrete roof over the road, closed on the mountain side. Stones and avalanches slide over the top of it.
82315.m: A gallery protects roads from stones and avalanches.

a: A large area of lying snow
An ice rink in the village
82316.e: A snowfield is a large area of snow in the mountains. It often stays until well into the summer.
82316.m: A snowfield is a large area of snow in the mountains.

82317.q: Why is there still snow on high mountains even in summer?
a: Because it is colder up there
Because the sun does not shine there
Because the snow there is salty
82317.e: The higher you go, the colder it gets. That is why the snow melts more slowly up there and stays.
82317.m: It is colder high up, so the snow stays longer.

82318.q: Why is a steep snowfield dangerous when hiking?
82318.e: Snow can be hard and slippery. If you slip, you can slide down the slope.
82318.m: You can slip on steep snowfields.

82319.q: How does old snow on a snowfield often feel in spring?
82319.e: Old snow thaws during the day and freezes again at night. This makes it grainy and wet.

82320.q: What can form from snowfields over many years?
82320.e: If snow stays every year, it gets pressed into ice under its own weight. This is how a glacier can form.
82320.m: Snow that stays can turn into a glacier.

82321.q: What protects your eyes on a bright snowfield?
82321.e: It is very glaring on a snowfield. Good sunglasses protect your eyes from the strong light.

82322.q: What does the meltwater from snowfields do in summer?
82322.e: In summer the snow melts slowly. The water flows into streams, rivers and lakes.
82322.m: Meltwater fills the streams in summer.

82323.q: Why do you get sunburnt quickly on snowfields?
82323.e: The bright snow strongly reflects the sunlight. That is why almost twice as much light hits your skin, and you need sun cream.
82323.m: On snow you need sun cream.

a: A deep shaft in the glacier ice
82324.e: A glacier mill is a round, deep shaft in the ice of a glacier. Meltwater swirls down it into the depths.
82324.m: A glacier mill is a shaft in the glacier ice.

82325.q: What grinds a round hole into the rock at the bottom of a glacier mill?
a: Swirling water with sand and stones
82325.e: The water plunges through the glacier mill right down to the rock. There it swirls sand and gravel round and round and so grinds out a round hole.
82325.m: Swirling water with sand and stones grinds round holes into the rock.

82326.q: Why is a glacier mill called a “mill”?
a: The water turns and grinds inside it
Flour used to be ground there
It has sails like a windmill
82326.e: In a glacier mill, the water swirls round and grinds sand and stones. That is like a mill.
82326.m: In a glacier mill, the water turns like in a mill.

82327.q: What often lies right at the bottom of a glacier pothole?
82327.e: The stones were turned round and round by the water for a long time. This ground them round and smooth.
82327.m: Round, smooth stones often lie in glacier potholes.

82328.q: What shape are the walls of a glacier mill?
82328.e: The swirling water melts and grinds the walls round and round. That is why they are round and smooth.
82328.m: Glacier mills have round, smooth walls.

82329.q: Why do you find round holes from glacier mills even where there is no glacier today?
a: There used to be a glacier there
82329.e: In the Ice Age there were glaciers in many places in Switzerland. When they melted, the round holes were left in the rock.
82329.m: Round holes in the rock show that there used to be a glacier there.

82330.q: Where does the water plunge to in a glacier mill?
a: Down to the rock bed under the glacier
82330.e: The meltwater flows over the ice into the glacier mill. Then it plunges down to the rock bed under the glacier.
82330.m: The water of a glacier mill plunges down to the rock bed.

82331.q: How long did the water take to grind a deep hole into the rock under a glacier mill?
82331.e: Rock is very hard. The water with sand and stones had to swirl round for a very long time before a deep hole formed.
82331.m: Deep holes in the rock took a long time to form.

82332.q: Which city is the well-known Glacier Garden in?
82332.e: The Glacier Garden is in Lucerne. There you can see traces of the Ice Age right in the middle of the city.
82332.m: The Glacier Garden is in Lucerne.

82333.q: What can you see in the rock at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne?
82333.e: In the Glacier Garden you can see big, round holes in the rock. These glacier potholes were drilled by the water of a glacier.
82333.m: You can see glacier potholes at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne.

82335.q: What was someone trying to build when the Glacier Garden was discovered?
82335.e: Josef Wilhelm Amrein-Troller wanted to dig a wine cellar. While digging, the glacier potholes came to light.
82335.m: The Glacier Garden was found while building a wine cellar.

82336.q: What can you get lost in at the Glacier Garden in Lucerne?
82336.e: At the Glacier Garden there is a maze with lots of mirrors. It is easy to get lost in it.
82336.m: There is a mirror maze at the Glacier Garden.

82337.q: Which famous monument with an animal is right next to the Glacier Garden?
82337.e: The Lion Monument is a dying lion carved into the rock. It is only a few steps away from the Glacier Garden.
82337.m: The Lion Monument is next to the Glacier Garden.

82338.q: What time do the glacier potholes in the Glacier Garden in Lucerne come from?
82338.e: The holes formed about 20,000 years ago. At that time it was much colder than today.
82338.m: The glacier potholes in Lucerne come from the Ice Age.

82339.q: What lay over today's city of Lucerne in the Ice Age?
82339.e: In the Ice Age the glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. There was thick ice over Lucerne too.
82339.m: In the Ice Age there was a glacier over Lucerne.

82340.q: In which Swiss city do two big erratic boulders, the Pierres du Niton, stick out of the lake?
82340.e: The two Pierres du Niton lie in the harbour of Geneva in Lake Geneva. A glacier carried them there from the Mont Blanc area in the Ice Age.
82340.m: The Pierres du Niton are in Geneva.

82341.q: Why is an erratic boulder called a “Findling” (foundling) in German?
a: It lies there out of place, as if found
82341.e: An erratic boulder is often made of a different rock from its surroundings. It lies there as if someone had put it down.
82341.m: An erratic boulder does not match the rock around it.

82342.q: Where in Switzerland can you find lots of erratic boulders?
82342.e: In the Ice Age the glaciers reached far into the Central Plateau. That is why there are lots of erratic boulders there.
82342.m: There are lots of erratic boulders on the Central Plateau.

82343.q: What can experts tell from erratic boulders?
a: How far glaciers used to reach
82343.e: Glaciers carried the boulders to their edges. That is why erratic boulders show how far the ice used to reach.
82343.m: Erratic boulders show how far the glaciers used to reach.

82344.q: How big can erratic boulders be?
a: Only as big as a pea
Only as big as an egg
Only as big as an apple
82344.e: Some erratic boulders are huge and weigh many tonnes. Some are as big as a house.
82344.m: Some erratic boulders are as big as a house.

82345.q: What is the technical name for a boulder that a glacier carried far from its home?
82345.e: Erratic means “strayed”. Such a boulder is like a stone that has strayed and lies far away from its home.
82345.m: A boulder like this is called an erratic block.

82346.q: How long does it take for a glacier to carry an erratic boulder a long way?
82346.e: Glaciers usually only flow a few metres to a few hundred metres a year. So for a long journey they need many hundreds of years or even longer.
82346.m: Glaciers carry erratic boulders very slowly.

a: A lake high up in the mountains
82347.e: A mountain lake lies high up in the mountains. It is often small, cold and clear.
82347.m: A mountain lake lies high up in the mountains.

82348.q: Why is the water in mountain lakes usually very cold?
a: It comes from snow and glaciers
82348.e: Many mountain lakes are filled by meltwater. Also, it is cool high up, so the water stays cold.
82348.m: Mountain lakes are cold because meltwater flows into them.

82349.q: What carved out many of the hollows for mountain lakes?
82349.e: In the Ice Age, glaciers ground hollows into the rock. When the ice melted, these hollows filled with water.
82349.m: Many mountain lakes lie in hollows that glaciers ground out.

82350.q: Which village in the Bernese Oberland is the well-known Lake Oeschinen near?
82350.e: Lake Oeschinen lies above Kandersteg. It is surrounded by high rock faces.

82351.q: Why are the mountains often reflected so beautifully in a mountain lake?
a: The water is calm and clear
The water is full of foam
The lake is made of glass
There are mirrors in the lake
82351.e: When there is no wind, the surface of the water is as smooth as a mirror. That is why you can see the mountains in it.

82352.q: What colour are some mountain lakes because of fine rock flour?
82352.e: Fine rock flour from glaciers floats in the water. It scatters the light, and the lake shines turquoise.
82352.m: Rock flour makes some mountain lakes turquoise.

82353.q: Which fish often lives in cold, clear mountain lakes?
82353.e: Trout like cold water with lots of oxygen. That is why they like living in mountain lakes and mountain streams.
82353.m: Trout like living in cold mountain lakes.

82354.q: Which mountain is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze and has a famous pyramid shape?
82354.e: The Matterhorn also stands near Zermatt. It is world famous for its pointed pyramid shape, but it is lower than the Dufourspitze.
82354.m: The Matterhorn is a neighbour of the Dufourspitze.

82355.q: Which pass do you take from Tiefencastel into the Upper Engadine to St Moritz?
82355.e: The road over the Julier Pass leads from Tiefencastel to Silvaplana in the Upper Engadine. From there it is not far to St Moritz.
82355.m: The Julier Pass leads into the Upper Engadine.

82356.q: In old legends, who threw the erratic boulders around the countryside?
82356.e: In the past, people did not know that glaciers had brought the stones. That is why legends told of giants or the devil throwing them.
82356.m: In old legends, giants threw the erratic boulders.

82357.q: Which plants often grow on a scree slope?
82357.e: On a scree slope there is little soil and the stones move. Only a few tough plants with long roots can grow there.
82357.m: Only a few tough plants grow on scree slopes.

82358.q: What is it called when water vapour cools and turns back into liquid water?
82358.e: When warm water vapour cools, little drops of water form again. This process is called condensation.
82358.m: In condensation, vapour turns back into water.
